Content_English: A video has gone viral on Facebook claiming that members of the Arakan Army crossed into Bangladesh while trying to capture a Myanmar national on the Bandarban border in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. They then attacked a Bengali family and were confronted by the Bangladeshi army.

Headline_English: Jamaat-e-Islami has installed idols at nearly 300 puja halls across the country
Content_English: A photocard with the message that idols will be made at about 300 puja mandap across the country under the initiative of Jamaat-e-Islami has been circulating on social media. A photocard from the daily 'Aajker Patrika' is seen being used in this news.

Headline_English: Pakistani actress Hania Amir refused to shake hands with popular Bangladeshi actor Hasan Masud
Content_English: Recently, some posts on Facebook are claiming that Pakistani actress Hania Amir did not want to shake hands with popular Bangladeshi actor Hasan Masud. The posts say that Hania Amir exchanged greetings with various artists during her visit to Bangladesh. At that time, she objected to shaking hands with Hasan Masud. It is claimed that Hania Amir looked down on Hasan Masud because of his dark complexion and called him a 'bodyguard'.

Headline_English: Chinese warships approaching Bangladesh
Content_English: Recently, a 14-second video was shared on Facebook claiming that Chinese warships were approaching Bangladesh in the context of a joint exercise between Bangladesh and the United States.

Headline_English: Bangladeshi plane crashes after being hit by US helicopter
Content_English: A video is being shared on Facebook claiming that a Bangladeshi plane crashed after being hit by an American military helicopter at Chittagong Airport. Some posts using the same video claim that it is a scene of a fire on an American military plane at Cox's Bazar Airport.

Headline_English: Demand to declare Shibir the winner in JACSU elections, otherwise, Jahangirnagar University will face dire consequences
Content_English: A photocard of the daily Kaler Kantho containing a statement by Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir's central president, Zahidul Islam, has been circulated online. It is being claimed that his statement is that he is demanding that the Shibir be declared the winner in the Jahangirnagar University Student Union (JUSU) elections. Otherwise, he is threatening bad consequences at Jahangirnagar University.

Headline_English: Sadiq Kayem injured in DUCSU elections
Content_English: A news report has spread on social media claiming that more than 50 people, including Sadiq Kayem, were injured in clashes between Chhatra Dal and Shibir during the DUCSU elections. Many people are sharing a video along with this news.

Headline_English: Butter showroom owned by Towhid Afridi looted
Content_English: A video of a Butter showroom being looted is being circulated on Facebook recently. The caption claims that this is a video of content creator Towhid Afridi being looted with the help of the administration after his arrest at his Butter showroom in Dhaka.

Headline_English: People's Rights Council attacks DMP office
Content_English: On August 29, during a clash between the Jatiya Party and the People's Rights Council, President of the People's Rights Council and former VP of DUCSU, Nurul Haque Nur was seriously injured in an attack by the army and police. In this context, a video has gone viral on Facebook claiming that party leaders and activists attacked the office of the DMP (Dhaka Metropolitan Police) Commissioner.

Headline_English: Army raids Nurul Haque Nur's house
Content_English: On Friday night, the party's president Nurul Haque Nur was injured in a clash between Jatiya Party and Ganadhikar Parishad activists after the army and police beat him up. After the incident, a video was shared on Facebook claiming that the DB and the army had raided Nur's house. In the raid, crores of taka illegally kept in his house were recovered.

Headline_English: Attack on Pakistan Embassy in Dhaka
Content_English: On August 23 this year, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar arrived in Bangladesh on a two-day visit. A video of the clash is recently circulating on Facebook regarding this visit. The caption of the video claims that 'In protest against the visit of the Pakistani Foreign Minister to Dhaka, thousands of ordinary people in Dhaka attacked and surrounded the Pakistani embassy.'

Headline_English: Chhatra League leader's body recovered
Content_English: Recently, some videos are being circulated on Facebook claiming that the body of a missing Chhatra League leader was found with his hands and feet tied on the roof of the Agricultural Bank in Gajra Bazar, Jamalpur. It is being claimed that he was the college branch Chhatra League leader. He was strangled with a rope and tied to a pole and killed.

Headline_English: Karnaphuli Tunnel bursts, water gushes out
Content_English: "Water is falling like a waterfall in the beautiful tunnel in less than three years," a photo card with the Janakantha logo and a picture of a tunnel-like place has been circulating on Facebook. This photo card is being shared on Facebook with the caption, "Karnaphuli Tunnel is crying in sorrow." That is, it is being claimed that the photo of the tunnel is a picture of the Karnaphuli Tunnel that was opened during the previous government.

Headline_English: Shishir Monir says the August 21 grenade attack scene was created with AI
Content_English: A comment by Supreme Court lawyer Advocate Mohammad Shishir Monir on a photocard of online news portal Dhaka Post regarding the August 21 grenade attack is being circulated on Facebook. It is being claimed that Shishir Monir said that the August 21 grenade attack scene was created using AI.

Headline_English: Shibir announces candidates, panel for first time in DUCSU elections
Content_English: Dhaka University Central Student Union (DUCSU) elections are going to be held again after a gap of six years. Dhaka University student organizations have already announced their candidates. In this regard, some posts are being shared on Facebook claiming that Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir has publicly announced candidates for the DUCSU elections for the first time. In this regard, the live pages of the media including BBC Bangla's Facebook page have claimed, 'This is the first time in independent Bangladesh that Chhatra Shibir is going to hold elections for the Dhaka University Student Union by publicly announcing a panel. Student leaders at that time said that although Shibir had secretly given panels in various elections, they were not seen campaigning openly.'

Headline_English: Vandalism and fire at advisor Asif Nazrul's house
Content_English: Several posts on Facebook are sharing videos of vandalism and fire at a house, claiming that this is an incident of arson and vandalism by Chhatra League members at the village home of Legal Advisor Asif Nazrul in Comilla.

Headline_English: Trainer dies in dolphin attack
Content_English: Jessica was an experienced marine animal trainer. Since childhood, her dream was to work with sea creatures and give them love. She started raising a baby orca, named Cairo. Cairo would come out of the water when she called him and captivated everyone in the show. But one day in 2025, before the show, Cairo's behavior suddenly changed. He started wandering around, breaking his own rules and suddenly attacked Jessica. Jessica was injured by the guru, and the trainers could not save her. This incident shows that no matter how much wild animals are trained, their true nature does not completely change. Jessica raised a baby orca thinking that it was the most harmless animal in the world and taught it various tricks. But one day, everything changed. When Jessica got into the water tank like every day, the orca's behavior was unusual. Instead of being calm, he suddenly attacked Jessica violently. In an instant, the water in the tank turned blood red and within moments, everything was over.

Headline_English: Alleged statement of celebrities giving money in actress Shaon's name
Content_English: Today is the 50th anniversary of the assassination of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his family. On this occasion, many personalities from the country's cultural sphere have posted tributes on Facebook. In response to these posts, a picture of an alleged statement from the private Standard Chartered Bank is being shared, claiming that actress Meher Afroz Shaon paid 20,000 taka to 9 people from the country's cultural sphere to post on Facebook on this day.

Headline_English: Taking tips from dead bodies
Content_English: "My father is dead, so I have to understand what property he has, so after his death, he is taking a tip from his father to sign the document," a video has gone viral on social media. Investigations have revealed that the name of the person is Md. Hossain Khan. He is the owner of Winmax Mobile. He has been suffering from paralysis for a long time. This video was recorded while collecting tips from him while selling a property.

Headline_English: Army clashes with Rokeya Hall students
Content_English: Two videos are circulating on Facebook claiming to be the recent clash between the army and students at Rokeya Hall.

Headline_English: A chest full of money was recovered from Samantha Sharmin's house.
Content_English: A video is going viral claiming to have recovered a chest full of money from the house of National Citizens Committee spokesperson Samantha Sharmin.

Headline_English: Money recovered from BNP leader Habibur Rahman Habib's house
Content_English: A video has gone viral on Facebook claiming that seven sacks and a chest full of money have been recovered from the house of BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia's advisor Habibur Rahman Habib. The video begins with footage from Ekattor TV. Here, a news reporter can be heard saying that RAB has arrested Habibur Rahman Habib from the capital's Mirpur area.

Headline_English: Looted weapons recovered from mosque after a year
Content_English: Some photos are being circulated on Facebook claiming that a large number of looted weapons have been recovered from a mosque in the capital's Khilgaon police station, a year after the mass uprising.

Headline_English: NCP's unconditional apology to Jamaat-Shibir
Content_English: A photo of a press release from the National Citizens Party (NCP) is being shared on Facebook, claiming that the party is offering an unconditional apology for the heated exchange of words with Jamaat-e-Shibir over the past few days.

Headline_English: Riyad, arrested for extortion in Gulshan, granted bail
Content_English: Recently, some posts on Facebook are claiming that Abdur Razzak bin Sulaiman alias Riyad, the expelled leader of the Bangladesh Democratic Students' Union, who was arrested for extortion in Gulshan, has been granted bail.

Headline_English: NCP's 7-point July Charter pledge
Content_English: A student-public uprising took place in Bangladesh in July-August 2024. After this uprising, a section of the students led by it formed a new political party, the National Citizens Party (NCP). Recently, a pledge titled 'July Charter Pledge', signed by the party's PAD and leaders, containing 7-point demands, is being circulated on Facebook.

Headline_English: DU VC makes hijab mandatory
Content_English: Recently, some posts on Facebook are claiming that the VC of Dhaka University has made hijab mandatory for girls.

Headline_English: Gulshan extortion case: Arrested Razzak is a member of the Police Reform Commission
Content_English: Five people have been arrested for allegedly entering the house of Shammi Ahmed, a former Awami League reserved seat MP, in the capital's Gulshan area and demanding a ransom of Tk 50 lakh. One of the five arrested is Abdur Razzak Riyad, a leader of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement and Bangladesh Democratic Students' Union. After the news of his arrest spread on Facebook and in the media, it was revealed that Abdur Razzak Riyad is a member of the Police Reform Commission.

Headline_English: Pregnant police officer killed in banned Chhatra League attack
Content_English: A photocard is being shared on Facebook in the style of Kaler Kantho. The photocard reads, "Four people, including a pregnant police officer, were killed in a militant attack by the banned Chhatra League and the Left Alliance on a police vehicle in Gopalganj."

Headline_English: Bangladesh returns money to Haj pilgrims for the first time
Content_English: Religious Affairs Advisor Dr. AFM Khalid Hossain has said that the remaining 82.89 million taka will be returned to 4,978 Hajj pilgrims who performed Hajj under government management. He said this at a press conference on the issue of Hajj management, achievements and planning for the next Hajj season in the conference room of the Ministry of Religion at the Secretariat on Sunday (July 13). Based on his statement, it is being claimed on Facebook that this is the first time in Bangladesh that Hajj pilgrims have been refunded their money.

Headline_English: Khatib, victim of mosque attack, dies in Chandpur
Content_English: Maulana ANM Nur Rahman Madani, the khatib of Professorpara Mollabari Jame Mosque in Chandpur city, was hacked to death on July 11 this year. Some posts circulating on Facebook regarding this incident are claiming that Maulana ANM Nur Rahman has died.

Headline_English: Sargis' statement on banning Chhatra Dal-Yubdal
Content_English: A photocard containing the statement of Jatiya Nagorik Party's chief organizer (northern region) Sarjis Alam regarding the banning of Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal is being circulated on Facebook. The photocard reads as Sarjis' statement, '"The party will not take responsibility for the individual, the party will only take a share of the donations. This donation will again come to Bangladesh through remittances from London. Our only demand now is to ban Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal."

Headline_English: Bangladeshis granted golden visa in UAE
Content_English: Recently, several media outlets in the country have been spreading the news on Facebook that a new type of Golden Visa is being introduced for Indians and Bangladeshis in the United Arab Emirates. This visa will be mainly nomination-based. As a result, huge investments in business or property will no longer be required to get the visa.

Headline_English: International Criminal Court meeting on Sheikh Hasina's case
Content_English: A video has recently been circulating on Facebook claiming that "the Netherlands International Criminal Court is holding a live meeting on the July Movement and the August 5 terrorist attack, including the Awami League President Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina case, and the current situation in Bangladesh."

Headline_English: Mashrafe has acted in an Indian web series
Content_English:
Recently, some posts about Mashrafe have been going viral on Facebook. Mashrafe was found in an Indian web series.” “Mashrafi left the cricket world and entered another world.” Mashrafe Mortaza plays the role of a Bangladeshi police officer in an Indian web series called “Farzi” released on the OTT platform Amazon Prime Video. It can also be confirmed from mainstream news media that Mashrafe is acting in the web series. 
According to reports published in some mainstream media in Bangladesh, an Indian web series called ‘Farzi’ was released on Amazon Prime Video on February 10. Mashrafe Mortaza plays the lead role in this series. This series is mainly made about fake Indian rupees. It shows that fake rupees enter India through various neighboring countries. Bangladesh is one of them.

Headline_English: Marriage breaks up after watching dance videos
Content_English: A dance video was recently shared on Facebook, claiming that the groom's father broke off the marriage after seeing the viral dance video of his daughter-in-law in Dhamrai.

Headline_English: Prayers allowed in Greece after 180 years
Content_English: Recently, some posts on Facebook claim that Muslims in Greece have been allowed to pray after 180 years. There has been no official mosque in the capital Athens since the founding of the modern Greek state. In November 2020, a government-approved mosque was inaugurated in Athens. As a result, Muslims in Athens have been allowed to pray legally in a mosque after a long time.

Headline_English: US warship seized by Houthis in Arabian Sea
Content_English: In the wake of the recent Israel-Iran conflict, a video has been circulating on Facebook claiming that “Iranian-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen have captured a US warship and several US soldiers in the Arabian Sea.” The video shows several soldiers kneeling on a ship with their hands raised above their heads.

Headline_English: Tk 40 million recovered from former advisor Nahid's house
Content_English: Recently, a video of money being recovered from underground has gone viral on Facebook. It is being claimed that 4 bags of money have been recovered from the house of Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP) and former advisor to the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology of the interim government. Some posts claim that 3.5 crore taka has been recovered, while others claim that 4.5 crore taka has been recovered.

Headline_English: Today on the streets of Israel, they are saying, "Stop the war, Iran, we apologize, we want peace, not war."
Content_English: The ongoing Iran-Israel war has been going on for a week. Both countries have been affected by mutual attacks in this war that has been going on for more than a week. Iranian missiles have penetrated Israel's air defense system and hit the country. In such a context, an 8-second video is being shared on Facebook, claiming that Israeli citizens are apologizing to Iran in the face of Iran's attack. In the video, a group of men and women can be heard saying, 'Iran! Stop the war, we are sorry, we want peace.'

Headline_English: An Indian smuggler was injured in the coup
Content_English: A video of various products being seized from a patient in a wheelchair has gone viral on Facebook. It is claimed that this is a video of a Bangladeshi injured in the July coup being caught at the airport with drugs while returning from abroad for treatment. The person in the video is an Indian citizen named Nazrul Haque, who was injured in the July coup. On March 17, 2025, he arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka from Kolkata, India, disguised as a patient.

Headline_English: Pakistan opens border to Iranians amid Iran-Israel war
Content_English: Recently, a 46-second video was shared on Facebook claiming that Pakistan has opened its borders to Iranians.

Headline_English: UN mission from Bangladesh temporarily suspended
Content_English: A message is being circulated on Facebook claiming that the United Nations has temporarily suspended its missions to all departments of Bangladesh's law enforcement agencies, police, and armed forces, citing their involvement in corruption, money laundering, disappearances, and murders. It is also being said that this will take effect from July 7.

Headline_English: 44 Awami League leaders and activists arrested in London on charges of sabotage
Content_English: The chief advisor to the interim government, Dr. Yunus, went to London on a four-day state visit on June 10, 2025. During this visit, Awami League leaders and activists staying in London protested in front of the hotel and airport where the chief advisor was staying. In this context, a video has been circulated on Facebook in which the police are seen handcuffing and arresting several white protesters.

Headline_English: Israeli warplane shot down by Pakistani missile
Content_English: Amid the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict, a Facebook post claiming to be from a newspaper called 'The Jerusalem Times' is claiming that Pakistan has also implicated itself in the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict. An Israeli F-35 fighter jet has been shot down by a missile fired from Pakistan.

Headline_English: Recognition of four national leaders including Bangabandhu as freedom fighters revoked
Content_English: A news report has been published in several media outlets across the country claiming that the 'heroic freedom fighters' recognition of four national leaders, including Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, who led the Liberation War, Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, M Mansur Ali, and AHM Kamaruzzaman, has been cancelled.

Headline_English: 'There will be a rush to hold elections in December..'— Dr. Yunus
Content_English: Recently, a photocard of the daily Kaler Kantho is being shared, claiming that the interim government's chief advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus has said about the newly launched new political party, the National Citizens Party (NCP), "If elections are held in December, there will be a rush, the students have formed a party, they should be given some opportunity to be well organized."

Headline_English: 210 pilgrims killed in Mauritanian Hajj plane crash
Content_English: In a few days, the Hajj, one of the most important religious rituals for Muslims, will begin. Pilgrims from different parts of the world have started traveling to Saudi Arabia to participate in the Hajj. In such a context, a 22-second video is being shared on Facebook, claiming that a Hajj flight from the African country of Mauritania to Saudi Arabia has crashed, killing 210 people from the country.

Headline_English: Torture of Bangladeshi patients in India
Content_English: A video has gone viral on social media claiming that Indian extremist Hindu terrorists are brutally torturing patients and their relatives undergoing treatment at a hospital, suspected of being Bangladeshis who had gone to India for treatment.

Headline_English: Former coordinator Rafi and his wife are victims of eve-teasing
Content_English: A photocard claiming that Khan Talat Mahmud Rafi, former coordinator of the anti-discrimination student movement and joint convener of the Bangladesh Democratic Students' Union, was a victim of eve-teasing while getting wet in the rain with his wife, has gone viral on social media.

Headline_English: Singer Mumtaz's house demolished
Content_English: On May 12, 2025, singer and former MP Momtaz Begum was arrested in a murder case. In this context, a video of a white house being demolished with an excavator has gone viral on Facebook. It is being claimed that this is the scene of the demolition of Momtaz Begum's house.

Headline_English: Selina Hayat Ivy granted bail
Content_English: Former Mayor of Narayanganj City Corporation (Nasik) Dr. Selina Hayat Ivy was arrested on May 9 (Friday) in multiple cases related to the murder and attack incident during the July coup. However, since Monday (May 19) night, some Facebook posts are claiming that she has been released on bail. In support of this, a photo card modeled after Jamuna TV has also been circulated. The photo card, dated yesterday, reads, 'MP Ivy released on bail.

Headline_English: BNP stage vandalized for insulting Ghulam Azam
Content_English: A video has gone viral on Facebook claiming that “Jamaat Shibir has broken the BNP stage for insulting Ghulam Azam.” The video shows a large number of people wearing Punjabis and caps moving towards a pandal and climbing onto the stage, vandalizing chairs and other items.

Headline_English: Tarique Rahman, a victim of police torture
Content_English: Recently, a photo is being shared on Facebook showing three men in police uniforms feeding a man lying on the floor something from a bottle. It is being claimed that the man lying on the floor is BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman.

Headline_English: UN issues arrest warrant for advisors
Content_English: Recently, some Facebook posts are citing 'UN directives' and claiming that all advisors will be arrested if the killing of 3,200 police officers is not brought to justice.

Headline_English: Russia and China concerned over Awami League ban
Content_English: A photocard with the name and logo of BBC Bangla has gone viral on Facebook, claiming that India, Russia and China have expressed concern over the ban on Awami League's political activities. The photocard features pictures of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Headline_English: Viral list claims 15 of 26 people killed in India were Muslims
Content_English: A list of those killed in a gun attack in Indian-controlled Jammu and Kashmir has gone viral on Facebook, claiming that 15 of the 26 people killed in the attack were Muslims. The viral posts cite Indian media outlet India TV as the source for the list.

Headline_English: Old man commits suicide by jumping under train
Content_English: An old man named Mir Ruhul Amin committed suicide by lying under a moving train at Arani railway station in Bagha upazila of Rajshahi last Monday. A story is circulating on Facebook about his suicide. It claims that the old man's wife died 8 months ago. After that, his two sons and two daughters, after keeping their father for a few days, no longer wanted to keep him. There was a lot of fighting over this. Even one night passed and the old man stayed in the yard all night and the boys did not open the door. On the morning of his death, the two sons had a big fight with their wives and asked him to leave. The boys also threw his belongings in the yard. After that, the old man had been sitting at the station since dawn. He did not eat anything. He lay down in front of a moving train in the afternoon.

Headline_English: Muslim woman's hijab removed in Uttar Pradesh, India
Content_English: A video is being shared on some posts by Facebook users in Bangladesh. The video shows six people walking around in the presence of two police officers. The caption of the video claims that a group of BJP supporters in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, India, rudely surrounded a Muslim woman and pulled off her hijab. The caption also says that the police made the accused walk around after arresting them.

Headline_English: Entering the war in Afghanistan on behalf of Palestine
Content_English: Israel is once again attacking the Gaza Strip in Palestine, violating the ceasefire agreement. In this context, a video has gone viral on Facebook, claiming that Afghanistan is fighting against Israel on behalf of Palestine.

Headline_English: Murder in Gaza: Palestinian journalist attacks US minister
Content_English: A 24-second video circulating on Facebook, centered on the ongoing Israeli-Palestinian conflict, claims that a Palestinian journalist jumped on and attacked a US minister after he approved the killing of Palestinian civilians.

Headline_English: 33 BGB members missing
Content_English: Recently, a claim that 33 BDR (now BGB) members are missing has gone viral on Facebook. It is said that these BGB members went missing while on a mission in the Naf River in Teknaf.

Headline_English: Bangladesh Army arrests four RAW agents
Content_English: Recently, a post went viral on Facebook claiming that four agents of India's intelligence agency 'RAW' were arrested by the Bangladesh Army.

Headline_English: The decision to issue passports to 69,000 Rohingyas was made during the Awami League government's tenure.
Content_English: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is visiting Bangladesh. Professor Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government, accompanied him on Friday and broke the fast with about 100,000 Rohingya refugees at the Ukhiya refugee camp in Cox's Bazar. In the context of these incidents, a photo card is being shared on Facebook, with the Daily Inquilab reporting that 69,000 Rohingyas in Saudi Arabia will receive Bangladeshi passports by June. The photo card is aimed at the current interim government and asks who gave Yunus' government the right to issue passports to the Rohingyas.

Headline_English: Muslim homes being demolished in India for selling beef
Content_English: A 30-second video is being shared on Facebook claiming that the 'radical' Hindu administration of Gujarat has demolished the homes of Muslims this Ramadan for selling beef in India.

Headline_English: 8 people, including former army chief, appointed as advisors
Content_English: An approval letter has been circulated on Facebook claiming that former army chief General Iqbal Karim Bhuiyan and several others have been nominated for the oath of office as advisors to the interim government.

Headline_English: Man involved in Dhanmondi 32 vandalism killed in mob lynching
Content_English: A photo of a man being chased by a group of attackers has recently gone viral on Facebook. It is being claimed that the victim of the chase was involved in the vandalism of Bangabandhu's house at Dhanmondi 32 and was killed in a public lynching.

Headline_English: Weapons recovered from RU camp/student room
Content_English: A one-minute video is being shared on Facebook claiming that the Bangladesh Army has recovered weapons from the room of the Shibir president in Rajshahi University's (RU) Nabab Abdul Latif Hall. Again, a fake Facebook page opened in the name of Daily Amar Deshre has shared the video claiming that the weapons were recovered from the room of the Chhatra Dal president in the same hall.

Headline_English: Awami League leader's daughter raped in Feni
Content_English: Three photos are being circulated on Facebook claiming that the daughter of a man named Mosharraf Hossain Badal was kidnapped and raped by some members of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement and Chhatra Dal. Badal is involved in Awami League politics in Feni's Sonagazi Upazila and is the UP chairman of Mangalkandi. The viral photos show Badal's wife and his daughter. Another photo shows a woman with her face blurred out lying on a hospital bed.

Headline_English: Journalist attacked by robbers on way to press conference late at night
Content_English: A news item titled 'Journalist Jasim kidnapped on way to Home Affairs Advisor's press conference' has been circulating on social media. However, no truth was found in this news item during the investigation. In addition, a photocard with the same title was circulated on the layout of the online portal 'Barta24'.

Headline_English: The house named 'Ajak Bhaban' belongs to the father of former advisor Nahid Islam.
Content_English: Recently, a photo of a building called 'Ajak Bhaban' located in South Banasree of the capital is being shared on Facebook, claiming that it was purchased by the father of recently resigned information advisor Nahid Islam for Tk 10 crore.

Headline_English: UN peacekeeping forces arrive in Bangladesh
Content_English: Sharing a report from India's Aaj Tak Bangla, various Facebook accounts in Bangladesh are claiming that UN peacekeeping forces are entering Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Acid thrown at Hindu girls for not wearing burqa
Content_English: A video has gone viral on Facebook claiming that Hindu women in Bangladesh are being attacked with acid for not wearing a burqa during the day. The 33-second video shows a young woman trying to cover her face with a bag in a rickshaw while several young men surround her and shout for water.

Headline_English: Death of ZI Khan Panna
Content_English: A claim has recently been circulating in threads claiming that ZI Khan Panna, the chairperson of the country's human rights organization Ain O Salish Kendra (ASK) and senior Supreme Court lawyer, has died.

Headline_English: Trump rejects UN report on Bangladesh
Content_English: A 2-minute and 6-second video of US President Donald Trump is being shared on Threads, claiming that Trump has canceled the UN Human Rights Council report that accused Sheikh Hasina. The viral video, which was posted on February 4, shows Trump signing an executive order to withdraw his country from the UN Human Rights Council, claiming that Trump has canceled the report on human rights violations in Bangladesh during the July-August uprising.

Headline_English: Trump's tweet calling Yunus a 'dictator'
Content_English: A three-minute video is being shared claiming that US President Donald Trump has tweeted about Bangladesh's chief advisor Muhammad Yunus. It is claimed that Trump has called him a 'dictator'.

Headline_English: Dr. Yunus's rural house burned down
Content_English: A post has gone viral claiming that the rural house of Dr. Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government, has been set on fire.

Headline_English: Chhatra League activist killed in army firing
Content_English: The Ministry of Home Affairs announced the start of a joint operation "Operation Devil Hunt" across the country from the night of February 8. In this context, a photo card titled "Chhatra League activist killed in army firing" was circulated on Facebook by Dainik Samakal.

Headline_English: Jahangir Alam leads rally against coordinators in Gazipur
Content_English: Recently, some videos claiming that locals of Gazipur, led by former mayor Jahangir Alam, have taken a stand against the coordinators have gone viral on Facebook.

Headline_English: There is currently chaos and chaos in the country.
Content_English: A video titled 'Currently, there is violence and chaos in the country' has gone viral, in which some youths are seen attacking with sticks, sharp weapons, and firearms.

Headline_English: BBC calls Hasnat Abdullah a 'terrorist'
Content_English: A clip from British media outlet BBC News is being shared on Facebook, claiming that the BBC has referred to Hasnat Abdullah, one of the coordinators of the anti-discrimination student movement, as a 'terrorist'.

Headline_English: Pakistan Army tweets about demolition of house number 32 in Dhanmondi
Content_English: The student crowd vandalized Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's house at Dhanmondi 32 on Wednesday night, citing a Facebook speech by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is in exile in India. At one point, a bulldozer was also used in the vandalism. It is being claimed that a tweet from the Pakistan Army's X account called Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman a "traitor" and expressed joy over the demolition of the house.

Headline_English: Government grants Tk 5,300 to bKash on the occasion of Shab-e-Barat
Content_English: A post is circulating on Facebook that the government is giving a grant of Tk 5,300 to everyone in the country on the occasion of the upcoming Shab-e-Barat.

Headline_English: Jamaat did not make any mistakes in 1971.
Content_English: Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman has said that Jamaat did not make any mistakes in 1971 – a photo card made in the style of the daily Amar Desh is available on Facebook. The photo card quotes Shafiqur Rahman as saying, “In the past days, the nation has been taught wrong history. Jamaat was not against independence. Jamaat’s top leaders are national heroes who participated in the 1971 war of independence. Although Professor Ghulam Azam was supposed to be given the title of Bir Pratik, it was not given for some unknown reason.”

Headline_English: Student arrested for burning Holy Quran at Rajshahi University
Content_English: Many reports have been published in the country's mainstream media, including Prothom Alo, about the arrest of a student on charges of burning the Quran at Rajshahi University. The title of Prothom Alo's report on February 4 is "A student arrested for burning the Holy Quran at Rajshahi University." But recently, a photocard using the Prothom Alo logo has been seen on Facebook, with a three-line headline with a one-line subheading. The subheading says, "He burned the Quran on January 12." The main headline says, "Farid, the coordinator and camp leader of the Quran burning incident at RU, was arrested, wanted to incite Hindu-Muslim riots."

Headline_English: Home Affairs Advisor says, we gave Farooq Khan the opportunity to run Facebook in prison on the condition that he speaks out against Sheikh Hasina
Content_English: Recently, a Facebook status against former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has been shared from a Facebook ID named 'Faruk Khan' which has gone viral. The status is being circulated as being from jailed Awami League leader and former minister Col. (Retd.) Faruk Khan. In this context, a photocard made in the style of Prothom Alo is available on Facebook. The photocard claims that in the context of this Facebook status, the Home Affairs Advisor said, "We gave Faruk Khan the opportunity to run Facebook from jail on the condition that he speaks out against Sheikh Hasina."

Headline_English: A century-old Shivlinga was found at Dhanmondi 32.
Content_English: Former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina was ousted from power in the face of a mass uprising and left for India on 5 August 2024. Then on 5 February 2025, she announced that she would join a virtual session with Chhatra League leaders and activists from India, in protest of which the July Revolutionary Alliance announced the 'Long March to Dhanmondi-32' program. The agitated students and public staged a massive protest at Dhanmondi No. 32 on the same night. At one stage, they vandalized and set fire to the house of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. A picture of a Shivling was shared on Facebook in connection with this incident. As a result of the alleged demolition of the house, this Shivling, which is about 300 years old, was found underneath it.

Headline_English: 'War of words' on Bangladesh-India border
Content_English: Tensions have been high along the Bangladesh-India border since the beginning of this month over the construction of a barbed wire fence by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF). In this context, a video has gone viral on Facebook. It is claimed that residents of the two countries engaged in a 'sound war' by playing loud music on sound boxes on the border between Chapainawabganj in Bangladesh and India.

Headline_English: Asif Nazrul came live and said about Dr. Yunus' arrest in Switzerland.
Content_English: Recently, a live video of Legal Advisor Dr. Asif Nazrul's speech is being circulated on Threads. It is being claimed that he went live and said that Dr. Yunus was arrested in Switzerland.

Headline_English: Former Justice Manik passes away
Content_English: On January 27, news of former judge Manik's death in prison went viral on Facebook. Some posts included his photo with this caption - "Justice 'Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik Saheb', a heroic freedom fighter of Ranangan in 1971, was systematically tortured and killed in prison by the illegal Yunus government!!" Three photos of Manik were also included with the posts. One of the photos was from the day of his arrest on August 23. The other is a normal photo from earlier. But one is of him in a hospital bed in a sick condition.

Headline_English: Elon Musk gets his hair cut by a robot barber
Content_English: Elon Musk gets his hair cut by a robot barber - Dainik Janakantha recently published a report claiming this. In the report, the media outlet wrote that Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is once again at the center of internet discussion. This time he surprised everyone by getting his hair cut by a robot barber. Recently, a video went viral on social media where a sophisticated robot is seen cutting Elon Musk's hair. On January 22 (Wednesday), the media outlet also published a photo card with this report on its verified Facebook page.

Headline_English: 18 Indian nationals killed on Bangladesh-India border
Content_English: Tensions have been high between the Bangladeshi Border Guard Force (BGB) and the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) since the beginning of this month over the construction of a barbed wire fence along the Bangladesh-India border. In the wake of this, a Facebook post in the form of a photocard claims, without citing any source, that one Bangladeshi was injured and 18 Indians were killed in clashes along the Bangladesh-India border.

Headline_English: Trump's big blow to Yunus! US President Trump stops sending all aid and money to Bangladesh
Content_English: Since Donald Trump took office as US President, the US State Department has suspended aid to many countries and has stopped approving new aid. This incident is being portrayed in various Indian media outlets and on Facebook as if Trump has only stopped aid to Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Bkash is giving a bonus of Tk 15,000 to its customers on the occasion of its 15th anniversary.
Content_English: A post is circulating on Facebook that says bKash is giving a bonus of 15,000 taka to all customers on the occasion of its 15th anniversary.

Headline_English: Sheikh Hasina, Tarique Rahman attend Trump's swearing-in ceremony
Content_English: Claims have been circulating on social media that Awami League President Sheikh Hasina or BNP Acting Chairperson Tarique Rahman attended the swearing-in ceremony of Donald Trump, the 47th President of the United States.

Headline_English: Coordinators attacked for extortion in Satkhira's Kachchi Dain
Content_English: A video posted on Facebook claims that shopkeepers are being beaten up by shopkeepers for demanding extortion after not paying the bill after a meal at a hotel in Kachchi Dain, Satkhira.

Headline_English: TikTok may be banned in Bangladesh
Content_English: Recently, some Facebook posts are claiming that the popular social media platform TikTok will be shut down from next Sunday. TikTok's parent company, China's ByteDance, has announced that it will shut down TikTok from next Sunday due to legal complications.

Headline_English: The army will now provide training in every school.
Content_English: "From now on, the army will provide training in every school" Recently, an anonymous photocard is being circulated on Facebook quoting the Home Affairs Advisor. A picture of the Home Affairs Advisor has been attached to it. On November 26, after discussions with officials from various departments of the administration at the Sylhet Circuit House, the Home Affairs Advisor of the interim government, Lieutenant General (Retd.) Md. Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, spoke to journalists on various issues related to national security. He also spoke about army training in schools.

Headline_English: The bird with fire flies from California to New York
Content_English: Recently, a picture of two birds has been circulating on Facebook claiming that the birds are flying from California to New York with fire. The two pictures were used in two different reports published in Amazing World and the Washington Post in 2021. Both reports were about the Australian bushfires. As a result, for good reason, the birds are flying to New York with the fire burning in Los Angeles.

Headline_English: Three Jamaat-Shibir members arrested in Jajira Police Station OC's death
Content_English: Police recovered the hanging body of Al-Amin, the officer-in-charge (OC) of Shariatpur's Jajira police station, on Thursday (January 9). In light of this incident, claims are being made on Facebook that the police have arrested three members of Jamaat-Shibir on charges of involvement in the death of OC Al-Amin.

Headline_English: Kolkata doctors announce 40 percent discount on medical services for Bangladeshi patients
Content_English: Recently, a photocard of Jamuna TV was shared on Facebook claiming that doctors in Kolkata have announced a 40 percent discount on medical services for Bangladeshi patients. After JN Roy Hospital in Maniktala, Kolkata, announced not to treat Bangladeshi patients in protest against the insulting of the Indian national flag, Behala Balananda Brahmachari Hospital in West Bengal announced a 40 percent discount for Bangladeshi patients. The thumbnail of a video on Jamuna TV reads, “They will see Bangladeshi patients” and the 40 percent discount

Headline_English: Indian-origin Ramaswamy appointed US ambassador to Bangladesh
Content_English: A post has been circulating on Facebook demanding that US tech entrepreneur and politician Vivek Ganapathi Ramaswamy be appointed as the US ambassador to Bangladesh. A press release from the US Embassy in Dhaka on Thursday (December 9) said that senior Foreign Service member Tracy Ann Jacobson will be the acting US ambassador to Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Chinese media declares Yunus government illegitimate
Content_English: "Chinese media outlet Xinhua has declared the Yunus government illegal" - such information has been circulating in various contexts since August last year. China's state-controlled media outlet Xinhua publishes news about Bangladesh quite seriously. In addition to political news, events such as the Bangladesh winter and trade fair are not left out. After the interim government took office, they have also published those news with great importance. However, they publish such news that the Yunus government is illegal. In addition, the country's mainstream media also publish such news citing Xinhua.

Headline_English: Shah Rukh Khan's wife Gauri's conversion
Content_English: Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan's wife Gauri Khan has converted to Islam and gone to Mecca with her family, some pictures of the couple have gone viral on Facebook. In the pictures, they are seen dressed in Hajj attire. Their son Aryan Khan is also present. Shah Rukh Khan's wife Gauri Khan has converted to Islam and gone to Mecca with her family

Headline_English: Jamaat leader expelled over Jira looting incident
Content_English: A photocard made in the style of the Daily Ittefaq, which expelled a Jamaat leader over the looting of a truckload of cumin seeds, has gone viral on Facebook.

Headline_English: Over 100 injured in DU Chhatra Dal attack, including VC and proctor
Content_English: A claim that more than a hundred people, including the university's vice-chancellor and proctor, were injured in the Chhatra Dal attack on Dhaka University (DU) on the night of January 2, 2025 has gone viral on Facebook. According to reports published in several media outlets in the country, students of the university protested at DU on the night of January 2 demanding an outline for the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU) elections. At that time, they accused the Chhatra Dal of obstructing the discussion on DUCSU at the syndicate meeting. Earlier, at 6 pm on Thursday (January 2), the highest policy-making forum of Dhaka University (DU) Syndicate meeting, Chhatra Dal leaders and activists protested and got into an argument with the Vice-Chancellor demanding that the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU) elections not be discussed and that no decision be taken quickly.

Headline_English: Pakistan Army to come to Bangladesh for training
Content_English: The claim that the Pakistan Army is coming to Bangladesh to train Bangladesh Army personnel has gone viral on various Indian media outlets and social media. Quoting unidentified sources, various Indian media outlets have claimed that a team of the Pakistan Army has been invited to train Bangladeshi soldiers. An officer of the rank of Major General of the Pakistan Army will supervise the training of Bangladeshi Army soldiers. The news outlets, citing unidentified sources, said, "The training will begin in February 2025. The first phase of the training will be held at the Army Training and Doctrine Command Headquarters in Momenshahi Cantonment. The first phase of the training will be completed within a year. Later, the Pakistan Army will train 10 more commands of the Bangladesh Army."

Headline_English: Asif Mahtab made advisor again
Content_English: Advisor Nahid Islam is being quoted on Facebook as saying that "the process of making Asif Mahtab an advisor is underway." Earlier, a fake post was viral on Facebook to replace Advisor Mustafa Sarwar Farooqui and appoint Asif Mahtab as an advisor. At that time, Asif Mahtab said in his Facebook post that he was unlikely to become an advisor. This time, there is no post on this matter from Asif Mahtab, Nahid Islam, or the press wing of the chief advisor. There is no news about this in the mainstream media either. Recently, the interim government's aviation, tourism, and land advisor AF Hasan Arif died, after which there are rumors of appointing a new advisor.

Headline_English: Trump imposes sanctions on 20 advisers, including chief adviser
Content_English: A photocard from Bhorer Kagoj has gone viral on social media. It is being claimed that Donald Trump has imposed sanctions on 20 people, including his chief advisor. However, the original report claims that the claim of sanctions is rather fabricated. But the headline of the report creates a kind of confusion.

Headline_English: Coordinator Sarjis Alam arrested
Content_English: Recently, it is being claimed on Facebook that Sarjis Alam, the central coordinator of the anti-discrimination student movement and the main organizer of the National Citizens Committee, has been arrested. This information was spread on Facebook on December 14, 2024. However, after this, Sarjis Alam's verified Facebook profile was seen to be regularly active. In a video on December 18, he was seen physically speaking about the clash between the two sides of the Tablighi Jamaat at the Ijtema ground. On the same day, he was also seen attending the press briefing on the student killings published on the verified Facebook page of the National Citizens Committee.

Headline_English: 150 people killed in clashes at Ijtema grounds
Content_English: Two groups of Tablighi Jamaat clashed over control of the Bishwa Ijtema ground in Tongi, Gazipur on Wednesday (December 18). Casualties also occurred in the clash. Claims are being made on Facebook about the incident that the death toll at the Ijtema ground is between 100 and 150. Regarding the clash, the interim government's Home Affairs Advisor, Lieutenant General (retd) Jahangir Alam, held a meeting with Saad and Zubayr supporters at the secretariat yesterday and informed journalists about the deaths in the clash.

Headline_English: All coaching centers in the country to be closed from January 1
Content_English: All coaching centers to be closed from January 1st - this information is being shared on Facebook. Apart from The Daily Campus, this information has also appeared in the headlines of two other newspapers. The Directorate of Health Education has decided to close all the activities of the coaching centers from January 1st to 17th to avoid the leakage of the question paper of the upcoming MBBS admission test on January 17th. There will be no more coaching centers from January 1st.

Headline_English: Taheri faces lawsuit over comments on Yunus' statement
Content_English: A claim has been circulating on Facebook that a false case has been filed against controversial speaker Mufti Gias Uddin Taheri for posting a status about the speech of the interim government's chief advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus. Basically, the police have filed a case against Taheri as the main accused in the attack on the police during a gathering in Akhaura, Brahmanbaria.

Headline_English: Arsenic found in sugar imported from India
Content_English: A report has been circulating on Facebook and threads that sugar imported from India contains arsenic, and that the Bangladesh Council for Scientific and Industrial Research has confirmed this information.

Headline_English: 4 Awami League leaders arrested in India for rape
Content_English: Several media outlets in India and Bangladesh have published reports demanding the arrest of four Awami League leaders on charges of rape in India. The claim was later spread on Facebook. These reports claim that they were arrested on charges of rape from a flat in Kolkata's New Town area last Sunday (December 8).

Headline_English: Quran is mandatory in schools and colleges – advisor speaks
Content_English: Recently, some posts on Facebook are quoting the religious advisor, saying - "Quran is being made mandatory in schools and colleges." Again, some posts are quoting advisor Asif, saying - "Quran education should be made mandatory in schools and colleges for Muslim students."

Headline_English: Banknotes with graffiti from the July Revolution are now on the market
Content_English: The interim government of Bangladesh has approved the printing of new banknotes with the design of 20 taka, 100 taka, 500 taka and 1000 taka banknotes. In continuation of this, a picture of a 100 taka note with graffiti of the July Revolution instead of the picture of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman has recently been circulated on Facebook. It is claimed that this is the new 100 taka banknote introduced by the interim government. The note is signed by Fazle Kabir, the current governor of Bangladesh Bank. The picture of the graffiti reading 'Tumi ke Ami ke Bikal Bikal' has been edited and added in that place.

Headline_English: Bangladesh bought Indian sugar from Pakistan
Content_English: Pakistani media outlet The News International reported on December 3 that Bangladesh has purchased 25,000 tons of sugar from Pakistan. Several claims are being made on social media regarding this sugar purchase from Pakistan - (1) Pakistan purchased 500,000 tons of sugar from India in the last fiscal year, from which Bangladesh is purchasing 25,000 tons, and (2) Pakistan imported sugar worth $3.56 million from India in August 2024 alone. Bangladesh is now importing that sugar at a higher price.

Headline_English: Anupam Sen forced to resign for being Hindu
Content_English: After retiring from Chittagong University, Anupam Sen had been serving as the Vice Chancellor of Chittagong's private Premier University since 2006. After serving for 18 years, the 84-year-old teacher resigned on December 6 citing old age. Since December 4, students have been protesting under the banner of "General Student Anti-Discrimination Student Movement, Premier University" demanding the resignation of the university's Vice Chancellor, Deputy Vice Chancellor and Treasurer. A total of five people, including the university's Deputy Vice Chancellor Kazi Shamim Sultana and Treasurer Towhid Sayeed, resigned; except for Anupam Sen, the remaining four are Muslims. Seeing Anupam Sen's Hindu name, the Indian media started spreading the news that the Hindu professor had been forced to resign.

Headline_English: Noor calls for attack on Indian High Commission
Content_English: In the wake of the recent attack on the premises of the Bangladesh Assistant High Commission in Agartala, India, a photocard made in the style of Prothom Alo is available on Facebook, in which the President of the People's Rights Council, Nurul Haque Noor, has called for an attack on the Indian High Commission in Bangladesh.

Headline_English: Tulsi Gabbard calls Chinmoy Krishna's arrest illegal
Content_English: Former ISKCON leader and spokesperson of Bangladesh Sammilit Sanatani Jagran Jote Chinmoy Krishna Das was arrested in Dhaka on November 25 (Tuesday) on a sedition case. He is currently in jail in Chittagong. Tulsi Gabbard has commented on Facebook regarding his arrest, claiming that he has been illegally arrested.

Headline_English: Shahid Nayan's return to the student movement against discrimination
Content_English: Nayan, a student from Tabgi Union in Borhanuddin Upazila of Bhola, was shot dead in Lalbagh, Dhaka, during the student movement against discrimination surrounding the quota reform movement in government jobs. He later died on August 9 while undergoing treatment at a private hospital. Recently, a photo of a couple is being shared on Facebook, claiming that Nayan, the martyr of the student movement, has returned. He is a resident of Ward No. 9 of Borhanuddin Upazila. The claim is being circulated on Facebook in written form without any photo.

Headline_English: Press release to ban ISKCON in the name of BNP
Content_English: A picture of a press release is being posted on social media, saying that BNP has issued a press release demanding a ban on ISKCON. The press release was issued by BNP.

Headline_English: Bangladeshi tank fleet heading towards Indian border
Content_English: Recently, a picture of a fleet of tanks is being spread on Facebook and X, claiming that Bangladeshi tanks are heading towards the Indian border. Later, it started spreading from Bangladeshi Facebook. The report published a report with the same picture. The title of this report is “Tank picture shows Bangladeshi tanks heading towards the Indian border”

Headline_English: Demands more bodies to be found if Chinmoy is not released
Content_English: Bangladesh Sammilit Sanatani Jagran Jote spokesperson and former ISKCON leader Chinmoy Krishna Das was arrested by Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) from the capital Dhaka last week. He was later taken from Dhaka to Chittagong and produced before the court. The court did not grant bail to Chinmoy Krishna Das and sent him to jail. However, due to the obstruction of his followers, chaos broke out in the court premises and a lawyer named Saiful Islam Alif was killed. A photocard with the name and logo of private broadcasting medium Soami TV has been circulating on Facebook in connection with this incident. The photocard uses the photo of an alleged ISKCON member and claims, “If the Lord is not released, 3 crore more bodies will be in the Sanatani field: ISKCON member warns in Facebook status.”

Headline_English: Indian satellite channels stopped broadcasting in Bangladesh
Content_English: Indian media outlet Republic Bangla has published a news story demanding that all Indian satellite TV channels be shut down in Bangladesh. The news has gone viral on Bangladeshi social media.

Headline_English: "You are next," warned Asif Mahmud, advisor to the interim government, writing:
Content_English: A Facebook post has sparked heated discussion and criticism. The main message of the post is that Asif Mahmud, an advisor to the interim government, has warned a newspaper by writing "You are next" on Facebook. The issue originated from a report published in the media.

Headline_English: New order to hang Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's picture in all courts in Bangladesh
Content_English: After the interim government of Bangladesh took office, pictures of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman have been removed from various important government offices. In this context, some videos with the logos of Boishakhi TV, Ekattor TV, Independent TV and My TV have been circulating on Facebook recently. It is being claimed that the High Court of Bangladesh has recently ordered the removal of pictures of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman from all courts in Bangladesh and the viral videos are part of the report in this regard.

Headline_English: Shahjalal International Airport renamed
Content_English: Recently, information has been circulating that the name of Shahjalal International Airport has been changed to Zia International Airport. Some people are posting old photos on Facebook along with the previous name.

Headline_English: Asif Mahtab appointed as advisor, replacing Farooqui
Content_English: Popular filmmaker Mostafa Sarwar Farooqui, the newly appointed advisor on cultural affairs to the interim government, has been replaced by former BRAC University teacher Asif Mahtab. According to the chief advisor's press secretary and media sources, Asif Mahtab confirmed the news of his appointment on his profile.

Headline_English: Solidarity with Mir Mughd, who was martyred on July 18, 2024
Content_English: On the night of November 20, Facebook suddenly started posting, "Mughd Ma'ra did not go, there was no one named Mugd! Mugd/Snigd were not two brothers, Mugd and Snigd were Snigd. The person was one!" The posts were spread almost simultaneously between eleven and twelve at night. Some IDs said, "Abu Saeed's grave is visited every two days, but Mugd's grave has not been visited even once! Mugd's Facebook ID name has been changed to Snigd. Even Mugd's parents did not file any case for Mugd's death! I heard that Shaheed Mir Mugd has finally returned in Snigd form!" If you keep an eye on the mainstream news media on July 18, there is no doubt that Mir Mugd was a martyr.

Headline_English: Advisor Mustafa Sarwar Farooqui resigns
Content_English: Filmmaker Mustafa Sarwar Farooqui was sworn in as the Cultural Affairs Advisor to the Interim Government on November 10, 2024. There has been much discussion and criticism on social media regarding the matter. Mustafa Sarwar Farooqui resigned from the Advisory Council. A statement was issued by the Interim Government. Meanwhile, on November 18, 2024, Cultural Affairs Advisor Mustafa Sarwar Farooqui met with the Chief Advisor to the Interim Government, Dr. Muhammad Yunus, and expressed his work plan.

Headline_English: 4.3 million TCB cards cancelled
Content_English: A news report was recently circulated in the media regarding the cancellation of 4.3 million TCB cards. The issue has been the subject of heated discussions and criticism on social media for a few days. One of the critics said, “TCB’s 4.3 million family cards have been cancelled. 4.3 million poor families have been deprived.” In light of these criticisms, Humayun Kabir, spokesperson for the government agency Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB), said that the cancellation of the cards is correct, out of 10 million family cards, 5.7 million cards have been converted into smart cards. The process of converting the remaining 4.3 million cards into smart cards is underway. Now the information is being updated and verified. Now all 10 million card holders are being given products.

Headline_English: Dr. Yunus asks to register for unemployment allowance
Content_English: A photocard modeled after Channel 24 has gone viral on Facebook, urging people to register quickly for unemployment benefits, said Dr. Muhammad Yunus, the chief advisor to the interim government.

Headline_English: Most of the women in Sylhet brothels are non-Muslims
Content_English: Recently, a post with pictures of several women and men and two police officers went viral on Facebook. The post claims that most of the brothels in Sylhet are neo-Muslim women.

Headline_English: Sheikh Hasina returns home in wake of Trump's victory
Content_English: A video of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina disembarking from a plane has recently gone viral on Facebook. The video is being shared claiming that Sheikh Hasina was able to return home because of the election of US President Donald Trump. The video also shows several people welcoming Hasina with flowers.

Headline_English: “I think Sheikh Hasina is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh” – Donald Trump
Content_English: A video of an interview Donald Trump gave to the PBD Podcast has recently been circulating on Facebook. It is claimed that Trump's comments are that Sheikh Hasina is still the Prime Minister of Bangladesh. In the original interview given to the PBD Podcast on October 17, 2024, the newly elected US President. There, he mainly spoke about the US border crisis, the voter ID law, Trump's past achievements in politics, the economy and business under Biden. He also spoke about Barack Obama, Kamala Harris, and his thoughts on the role of mainstream media in shaping public opinion.

Headline_English: Former soldier admits to using sniper rifle in protest
Content_English: A video has gone viral on social media Facebook, with the caption “Finally admitting to using sniper (7.62) in student protests.” The video shows a young man wearing a black T-shirt and cap talking about a certain topic. It is also clear from watching the video that it has been made up of fragments.

Headline_English: Hindu youth killed in army firing in Chittagong
Content_English: On September 5, clashes broke out over an anti-ISKCON Facebook post by a businessman in Hazari Lane, Chittagong. Amidst this tension, six patrol teams of army, police and BGB members reached the area. When the angry locals and Hindu community tried to stop the clash, acid was thrown at the members of the joint force. Apart from the detention and arrest, no reports have been published anywhere about the deaths. Meanwhile, on September 6, two college students named Amit Sutradhar and Abdullah Al Sayem died in a road accident in Moulvibazar.

Headline_English: Actress Mehjabeen was physically attacked
Content_English: A picture of actress Mehjabeen Chowdhury has gone viral on social media Facebook. It shows the actress with injury marks near her eyes and a bandage on her head. Many people posted the picture and wrote in the caption, Mehjabeen Chowdhury has been attacked by fundamentalists.

Headline_English: The interim government introduced banknotes without the image of Sheikh Mujib.
Content_English: Since the interim government took office in Bangladesh, there has been a rumor of canceling all bank notes with the image of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. In continuation of this, recently, pictures of two bundles of 100 taka paper notes without the image of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman have been circulating on Facebook. It is being claimed that these are the new 100 taka banknotes without the image of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman introduced by the interim government.

Headline_English: Inani Jetty, a waterway to St. Martin, was deliberately demolished
Content_English: Recently, a message has been circulating in threads that the only shipping route to St. Martin, Inani Jetty, has been demolished. However, as you know from various information and data, Inani Jetty is not the only shipping route to St. Martin. Rather, commercial tourist ships bound for St. Martin will start operating from this jetty in early 2024. Earlier, the ship MV Karnaphuli Express used to operate from BIWTA Jetty in Cox's Bazar city to St. Martin.

Headline_English: "A group that has received the good news of Paradise" is written on Jamaat's associate member form
Content_English: A photo is circulating on Facebook claiming to be an associate member of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. In this form, Jamaat-e-Islami is claimed to be the "party that has received the good news of Paradise."

Headline_English: Israel's defense chief killed in Hezbollah drone attack
Content_English: Recently, a news story has been circulating on Threads claiming that the head of the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF), Harji Halevi, has been killed in an attack by the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah. The claim that Harji Halevi was killed is true. Originally, on October 13, 2024, some Israeli soldiers were killed in a Hezbollah drone attack.

Headline_English: Chief Advisor hospitalized
Content_English: A picture of an ICU and a list of doctors are being advertised that the chief advisor has suffered a heart attack. A medical board has been formed for him. The doctors on the board are heart and ICU specialists. The Department of Anesthesia, Analgesia and Intensive Care Medicine of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University has instructed to keep an ICU bed ready at all times to ensure the emergency medical management of the chief advisor.

Headline_English: Dr. Muhammad Yunus, chief advisor to the interim government, resigns
Content_English: Recently, a picture of the interim government's chief advisor Dr. Muhammad Yunus and Army Chief Waqar-uz-Zaman has been circulating on threads. The caption of the picture claims that Dr. Muhammad has signed a resignation letter to Waqar-uz-Zaman. As a result, martial law has been imposed across the country.

Headline_English: Tesla Pi satellite phone release announcement
Content_English: Recently, social media threads have been claiming that Tesla's groundbreaking smartphone is coming to the market. It will be released by the end of the year under the name "Tesla Pi Phone" and will have three special groundbreaking technologies. This phone will never need to be charged, will be automatically recharged with solar energy, will not need the Internet as it is directly connected to Starlink, and will also be able to communicate with Earth, the Moon, and Mars.

Headline_English: Asif Nazrul announces Bangladesh's new Victory Day on July 36
Content_English: July 36th (i.e. August 5th) will be made Bangladesh's new Victory Day - a news story and photocard that incorrectly quotes Advisor Asif Nazrul has been circulating.

Headline_English: Chief advisor demands to leave country due to conflict with army chief
Content_English: A video circulating on Facebook claims that the advisors left the country due to disagreements with the army chief over various issues.

Headline_English: Armed attack by coordinators on advisor Sakhawat Hossain
Content_English: Multiple Facebook IDs and pages have claimed that the coordinators carried out an armed attack on Brigadier General (retd) Dr. M Sakhawat Hossain, former Home Affairs Advisor and currently the Advisor in charge of the Ministry of Textiles, Jute and Shipping.

Headline_English: Islamic speaker Taheri dies
Content_English: A photocard with the Channel 24 logo is circulating on Facebook, stating that Islamic speaker Taheri was injured in an attack on his car and died on the way to the hospital.

Headline_English: Army battles with advisors at government residence Jamuna
Content_English: Job seekers protesting to raise the age limit for applying for government jobs to 35 surrounded the official residence of the Chief Advisor on Jamuna on September 30. Earlier, the protesters, who had gathered at Shahbagh and taken out a procession, were stopped by the police with barricades when they reached Jamuna. Later, the police fired several rounds of tear gas to disperse them. Several protesters were killed in the process.

Headline_English: Chhatra League activist murdered at Geneva Camp in Mohammadpur
Content_English: A video has gone viral on Facebook claiming that a Dhaka University Chhatra League activist was slaughtered and killed at the Geneva Camp in Mohammadpur yesterday.

Headline_English: Abu Saeed dies after being hit in the head by a brick

Headline_English: Eating mango and drinking soft drinks can cause death

However, FactWatch spoke to an expert on the subject and found that there is no harm in consuming mangoes and soft drinks together, and the small amount of citric acid in mangoes does not react much with the phosphoric acid in soft drinks. However, citric acid and phosphoric acid are not allowed to be used together as food additives because they react in large quantities. Earlier, a post had spread that consuming jackfruit and Coca-Cola together could cause poisoning equivalent to the bite of three snakes and could lead to death, and FactWatch refuted that claim. Not only in Bangladesh, but in several countries in India, Thailand, and Africa, it was claimed that consuming mangoes, jackfruit, and durian (Singapore's national fruit) and drinking soft drinks could cause poisoning in the body.

Headline_English: Opportunity to become a citizen of Saudi Arabia under certain conditions

Headline_English: In Japan, you have to pay taxes for being overweight.
Content_English:
Under the “Metabo Law” enacted in Japan in 2008, anyone who is overweight will have to pay a tax. In order to reduce obesity in Japan, a law called “Metabo Law” was passed in January 2008, where women and men aged 45 to 74 were asked to measure their waistline once a year and if someone’s waistline is more than the specified range, they will have to pay a tax. If institutions and local governments cannot manage the obesity of their citizens/employees, those institutions or local governments will have to pay a fine. There was a provision to pay a tax or fine to obese people. 
Basically, the name “Metabo Law” comes from metabolic syndrome, which refers to high blood pressure, high blood sugar, excess body fat, and abnormal cholesterol levels in the body, which can cause various heart diseases, stroke, diabetes and other complex diseases. In Japan, people are trying to avoid fat to avoid metabolic syndrome and to comply with the government's ideal waistline standard, according to a report published on November 10, 2009 by the US-based public radio news program The World. The article also noted that Japanese lawmakers have set a maximum waistline size for men and women over the age of 40, at 85 centimeters (33.5 inches) for men and 90 centimeters (35.4 inches) for women.

Headline_English: The rate of hired workers at BNP's rally is 400 for men and 600 for women.

It is known that those youths participate in organizational and social events such as movements, protest rallies, human chains, seminars, etc. in exchange for money. 

On condition of anonymity, a young man was spoken to in the Paltan area of ​​the capital. His name is Ahsan Habib (pseudonym); he graduated from a college in the capital. He has given interviews to many private organizations for jobs. Due to lack of experience and recommendations, the rate of hired agitators is 400 for men and 600 for women. 

He complains that he has not been given a job. He is also taking exams for jobs in various government departments. Since his family could no longer meet his expenses, it became difficult for him to continue trying for a job in Dhaka. In this situation, he learned from a friend in the mess that money can be earned by participating in various programs. Then he joined a group centered around Paltan-Press Club and took part in this work. 

Ahsan Habib told Desh Pantar, ‘I am doing this work out of compulsion. It is not that one can earn much here. Some days I get 700 taka, some days I get 150 taka. If I come and sit, I can't get work. When people are interested, the leaders contact me through various links. Later, many people like me are called through various groups and informed about the place and time of attendance. Then we go there. I try not to go to political programs, because there is a risk of getting caught.' 

Another young man spoke, keeping his identity secret. His name is Saiful Islam (pseudonym). He said, 'I work part-time in an event management company. There is not always work there. So I come to various programs through an older brother I know. Although there is not always work. But the money I get is not bad.' 

The investigation revealed that numerous young people like Ahsan Habib are waiting to participate in such work in the Paltan, Press Club and Gulistan areas of the capital. There is another circle active around them; who maintain contact with young people like Habib and coordinate with the leaders of various parties and organizations. In return, they take one to one and a half hundred taka per person. Women also participate in these groups. Women are in high demand for various programs, and they have to pay extra money per person. 
A broker was found in the Press Club area of ​​the capital undercover. His name is Md. Helal. He is one of the controllers of hired workers in the National Press Club area. Talking to this middle-aged man, it is learned that he has been involved in this work for a long time. Helal told this reporter that for a one- to one-and-a-half-hour program, the minimum payment is 150 taka. For a day-long program, the minimum payment is 400 taka per person. Women are in high demand, so they have to pay 600 taka. He gets a part of this money. Now, the demand for people has increased due to the elections. However, if the money is increased, a lot of people can be found. He said, "I can easily get 150-200 people. Even if it takes more, I can, but I have to tell you the time and number of people." 

It is known that at least five groups that rent workers under verbal contracts are active in the National Press Club area alone. Various events of various organizations, including political and social, are held in this area throughout the year. As a result, their demand here is much higher than in other areas. If someone needs a hired worker, they come here and look for him. It can be said that the culture of hiring workers has developed from this area. And unemployed youth, students and young people involved in various part-time jobs join the work of hiring through brokers. Many others have taken it as a profession. Many drug addicts also participate in various programs for hire. 

Human rights activist Nur Khan Liton told Desh Vantar, ‘As long as the practice of lack of ideals continues, such practices will continue. It is not good for the country, the nation, or the society. Politics is now in the hands of miscreants, and the place of ideals in politics is weak. In such a situation, such incidents will happen, but it should not happen.’

Content_English: An Indian named Pandit Keshav has filed a case against World Cup-winning Australian all-rounder Mitchell Marsh. Headline_English: Eating meat from animals slaughtered according to halal methods causes cancer
Content_English:
A rumor has been circulating on social media that when an animal is slaughtered in a halal manner, a deadly hormone called strychnine is released in its meat in large quantities, which is responsible for cancer. 
This video was uploaded by an unverified page named Supriyo Live at 9:44 pm on October 10. In the original video, a restaurant employee is seen talking to a customer about “halal” meat and “jhatka” meat supplied to an Indian restaurant. Here, the customer claims that I have a lump in my throat. I will not eat halal meat (slaughtered according to Muslim customs due to religious beliefs). Give me jhatka food (a method of preparing meat by cutting the head off the animal’s body in one fell swoop). 
Unknowingly, we are being fed only halal food. With a swollen chest as usual. 

Know one truth, when an animal is slaughtered in a halal manner, a deadly hormone called strychnine is released in its meat in large quantities. This strychnine hormone causes most cancers.

Headline_English: Pakistan-Bangladesh are brothers against India, Islamabad's plan for a secret agreement with Yunus
Content_English:
A new twist in South Asian geopolitics? Speculation is growing over a proposed secret defense agreement between Pakistan and Bangladesh. According to sources, this potential defense deal is not limited to the boundaries of bilateral relations alone. Rather, the issue is very sensitive in terms of India's strategic interests as well. Let's understand the whole thing in simple terms. 

In the past few months, high-ranking Pakistani military and intelligence officials have visited Dhaka one after another. The chairman of Pakistan's Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee, the chief of the Navy, and even Lieutenant General Asim Malik, the head of the notorious intelligence agency ISI, have also visited Bangladesh. Although these visits are officially called 'courtesy', according to a section of diplomatic circles, there may be a well-planned agenda behind it. 

Sources claim that Pakistan wants to sign a NATO-style mutual defense agreement with Bangladesh. That is, an attack on one country will be considered an attack on both countries. Pakistan recently signed such an agreement with Saudi Arabia. Security analysts interpreted that agreement as an attempt to create a strategic balance against India. Now, Islamabad is trying to bring Bangladesh to its side using that model.

Headline_English: Salman F. Rahman can't read Bengali!

Besides, two are sleeping on the floor of the DB jail.
