Headline_English: "There is nothing more cruel than love."
Content_English:
Kangana Ranaut, who is now a member of parliament, has been elected to parliament from Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, on behalf of the BJP. The new member of parliament has called love cruel, citing an incident. 

Recently, Kangana got emotional after seeing the picture of the widow of the country's late soldier Anshuman Singh receiving the medal. She shared a picture on her Instagram story. In the picture, Anshuman Singh's wife is seen receiving the medal on his behalf. 

Posting the picture, Kangana wrote, 'Many soldiers gave their lives for this country. They were awarded yesterday. But people's eyes have come to tears after seeing the picture of Anshuman Singh's wife from the eastern region receiving the award.' 

Kangana also wrote, 'She still loves her husband very much. She cried while holding this medal in her chest. 

This video of hers still hurts me. Love is not easy; Rather, the funny thing is that there is nothing more cruel than love.’ 

At that event, Captain Anshuman Singh was posthumously awarded the Kirti Chakra. His wife accepted it. The late Anshuman was awarded the award for saving the life of a colleague in a recent fire. The Kirti Chakra award is India’s second highest peacetime hero award.

Headline_English: Ronaldo's six, 3 Saudi League players in Portugal
Content_English:
Although England and France are the favourites for the upcoming Euro Championship, there is no way to keep Portugal behind. The team's coach Roberto Martinez announced a 26-member squad on Tuesday for the European Championship to be held in Germany next month. The team that is expected to have a place is Cristiano Ronaldo, Bernardo Silva, Rafael Leao, Bruno Fernandes, Ruben Dias, Vitinia, Diogo Jota, Joao Felix. 

Ronaldo played his first Euro in 2004. He was an important member of Portugal in all four tournaments held since then. He also won the title in Euro 2016. With the call-up to this team, the former Real Madrid star is going to play six Euros. 

However, Ronaldo already has a record in the Euro. He played a maximum of 25 matches in the tournament. In addition, the 39-year-old superstar also holds the record for the highest goal scorer with 14 goals. This time, the record for the most Euro games was also broken last time, this time Ronaldo will go further by scoring 'six'. 
It is not just Ronaldo who has got a place from the Saudi Pro League. Ronaldo's Al Nasr teammate Otavio Monteiro is also in the Portugal team. In addition, Martinez has also kept Al Hilal midfielder Ruben Neves.

Headline_English: 400 games for men, zero for women
Content_English:
The Taliban have approved 400 sports that do not conflict with Sharia law. However, these are only for men. The Taliban's new sports chief has expressed his inability to answer what sports are available for women. 
Several new announcements have been made since the Taliban came to power in Afghanistan. Meanwhile, on Tuesday (September 14), Afghanistan's new sports chief Bashir Ahmed Rustomzai said that men will be able to play 800 sports that support Sharia. When asked about their decision on women's right to play, he told AFP, "Please don't ask me about women." 

A student at Kabul University. Photo: Collected 

Rustomzai, a champion in kung fu and wrestling, has been appointed as Afghanistan's director general of sports and physical education. After the Taliban came to power for the second term, Rustomzai said, "We will not ban any sport as long as it is against Sharia law." 400 types of sports are approved here. 

He said he is waiting for instructions from the Taliban's top leadership on women's participation in sports in Afghanistan. 

According to Rustomji, the sports for men will not change much. For example, shorts must be knee-length when playing football or boxing. He said that increasing the length of the shorts will not have much impact on the style of play.

Headline_English: Praying at the top of a palm tree!
Content_English:
A young man named Abdur Rahim (28). On Monday (March 1) afternoon, a scene of offering prayers on top of a palm tree in Kuthipara village of Tanor municipality in Rajshahi created a sensation in the area. 

After offering prayers, he raised the national flag of Bangladesh on the tree to show respect to the martyrs. Hundreds of people in the area stood and watched this scene while Rahim offered prayers. Abdur Rahim is a resident of Mougachi village of Mohanpur upazila. Rahim was born in Bogra. However, he came to Mohanpur, Rajshahi and got married and has been living there for several years. Bangladesh News

Meanwhile, after finishing the prayers, Abdur Rahim came down from the palm tree and said, "I climb various trees, including palm trees, at the risk of my life and show sports. But before that, I offer two rakat prayers on the tree to please Allah. I also play some sports. Seeing all this, people give me some money. I run my family with that.

It is known that Abdur Rahim, in addition to performing prayers, also spoke to the people present. After that, he showed some physical exercises and descended from the tree.

Locals said that Abdur Rahim regularly performs prayers. He recites poetry and performs jharfung. Rahim performs prayers on a date palm tree and also performs physical exercises there. He sometimes performs prayers by climbing various trees including date palm trees and shows sports on the trees. Rahim has been doing all this since he was a child.

When asked about performing prayers on a date palm tree in this way, Dr. Sakhawat Hossain, a prominent Islamic thinker and researcher from Rajshahi, said that this is nothing but madness. There is no example of performing prayers on a date palm tree or any special virtue of it in any of the rules of Islam.

Headline_English: He is an engineer, she is a doctor!
Content_English:
One identity card says - Engineer Mohammad Shahriar, Assistant Engineer, Capital Development Authority. However, his other identity card shows that he is a doctor! Is that all? He is an officer of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) and Resource Integration Center (RIC). He is also the health editor of a newspaper. He has many names like fake identities. He had been committing various frauds under these names and identities. Finally, Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Police (DB) arrested him from Jatrabari area of ​​the capital on Wednesday. 

Additional Deputy Commissioner in-charge of Web Based Crime Investigation Team of DB's Cyber ​​and Special Crime Division Md. Ashrafullah told Samakal that the arrested youth used to introduce himself as a doctor and prepare fake medical reports for people going abroad. He introduced himself as Hafizul Islam Sardar alias Dr. Shafiq Shahriar alias Md. Shafiq alias Md. Mamun. He uses different names and identities for various frauds. Sometimes he also introduces himself as a journalist. A case was filed against him at Jatrabari Police Station on Thursday. 

The DB official said that 12 visiting cards of doctor's identity, 45 blank pages and 80 envelopes of People's Digital Diagnostic Center and Consultation's lab report writing pad, five pages of blank pads of legal notices with ACC logo and watermark, 10 forms of BRTA's temporary permit, 131 stickers of various televisions, three fake seals of various BRTA departments, five cards of ACC, RAJUK, BRTA, RIC official identity, date changeable seals, etc. were found from the arrested youth. 

Quoting the initial interrogation of the arrested youth, the DB said that he made fake identity cards and pads from a computer shop of a certain Shafiq in Konapara, Demra and various presses in the Dainik Bangla Mor area. Then he used these in fraud and forgery. His main objective was to extort money through various tricks. He used the identities of several newspapers and TV channels to throw dust in the eyes of the law enforcement agencies. He has made a large number of stickers of various TV channels for use on vehicles. It is expected that details about his fraud tactics will be known during the interrogation on remand.

Headline_English: 'Sabotage' disappears during Eid holidays!
Content_English:
After the fire that destroyed Bangabazar and New Supermarket in the capital, the word 'sabotage' was being loudly chanted in political circles. The leaders and ministers of the government party said that they would investigate whether BNP-Jamaat was involved in it or not. They did not stop there. They also presented statistics on when and where BNP-Jamaat leaders and workers set fires and burned people. In response, the BNP leaders said that Awami League people set fires. 

According to the Sangsad Bangla dictionary, the word 'sabotage' means destruction, terrorism, conspiratorial activity, sabotage, etc. The English word sabotage is used to mean war, strike, sabotage, sabotage, sabotage, sabotage; intentional damage to machines, equipment, etc. 

On April 4, a fire broke out in Bangabazar and destroyed about 3,000 shops. After 11 days, 250 shops on the third floor of the New Supermarket burned down. The traders of the two markets have been completely destroyed in this fire. At this time, their rehabilitation and financial assistance were urgent. The government and various organizations have also provided assistance as much as they can. 

But what have our political parties done? While the affected traders of Bangabazar have started trading again to get a place to stand, the leaders of the government and opposition parties have become busy finding a solution to the sabotage. I have not seen any top leader of any party other than Jatiya Party chief Golam Quader go to the spot. Even the leaders of the left party did not feel the need to stand by the affected traders. They think that the fire problem will not be solved unless the bourgeois state system is broken. 

Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader said that BNP is again planning arson attacks ahead of the next national elections. He has instructed Awami League leaders and workers to guard the markets. On the other hand, the BNP Secretary General said that Awami League is the mastermind behind all arson attacks. He alleged that the Awami League is putting the blame on the neck of the Buddha to divert the attention of the people from the movement to restore democracy. 
If the Awami League leader thinks that the fire will stop if the party leaders and workers stand guard, then why didn't he send them there so far? The upcoming elections are also behind the fire and controversy between the two parties. All the controversies, quarrels, and clashes about the elections are happening in this country. To make the elections fair, politicians once added a caretaker system to the constitution and then canceled it again. But the Supreme Court said that if the parliament wants, the two elections can be held under the caretaker government. 

When the political leadership keeps blaming each other for the fire, let's see what the real situation is? Prothom Alo quoted the Fire Service as saying that the main reason for fires in the country is electrical faults. In 2022, 38 percent of the 24,102 fire accidents were caused by electrical faults. (Prothom Alo, April 20, 2023) 

According to the fire service, the second biggest cause of fire incidents is burning bits of bidis and cigarettes. In 2022, this accounted for a little over 16 percent of fire incidents. About 14 percent of fire incidents occurred from stoves. It can be electric, gas or earthen stoves. Gas supply lines are also a significant cause of fire incidents. In 2022, a little over 3 percent of fire incidents occurred from gas supply lines. Electrical disturbances, burning bits of bidis and cigarettes, stoves and gas lines accounted for 71 percent of fire incidents in 2022. Apart from this, children playing with fire, hot ashes or fuel, use of open flames, fire from vehicle accidents, etc. are the causes of fire incidents. In total, 19 causes have been found. 

Traders were crying loudly as they saw the present and future burning before their eyes 
The Dhaka South City Corporation's investigation into the Bangabazar incident has revealed that the cause of the fire was burning cigarette butts or a burning coil to repel mosquitoes. The report of the investigation committee into the fire at Dhaka New Supermarket on April 15 has not yet been received. However, Market Owners Association President Md. Shahidullah said, "The City Corporation people were working to demolish the bridge at around 3 am. They did not notice that we have a power line there on the bridge. The fire started when the bulldozer was running on that line." 

In Dhaka, the fire service responded to 16 such fire accidents in the last one and a half months (March 1 to April 18). The cause of seven of them has been known. Four occurred due to electrical faults. Two incidents occurred due to the accumulation of gas emitted through a gas line. These incidents were the explosions in front of Dhaka's Science Laboratory and Siddiq Bazar in the first week of March. 32 people died in them. Apart from this, the fire service said that a cigarette caught fire in a building in Rampura. Sometimes, accidents also occur due to equipment in the power supply system. The Fire Service says that a building caught fire after a transformer exploded in front of the Wari police outpost in Dhaka last Sunday night. No one was injured in the incident. Earlier, on April 1, three people died in a fire after a transformer exploded in Sweeper Colony near the Joykali temple in Wari. 

Where did the leaders of the government party get information about sabotage? The Fire Service investigation revealed that the main cause of the fire was electrical disturbance. If someone from the BNP or any other party sabotages, it is the government's responsibility to take legal action against them. If they do not do that, if they continue to wave their swords in the air, the fire will not be extinguished, nor will the cause be known. It must be admitted that the infrastructure of our markets is at least weak. The service lines are risky. Accidents can happen at any time. 

There are various stories about the government discovering sabotage. During the previous Awami League government, a case was filed against BNP leaders for the collapse of an electricity tower. Again, during the BNP government, a story of Jajmia was fabricated in the case of the August 21 grenade attack. 

Last year, after the police were attacked, bricks thrown and vandalized during the clash between students and businessmen in New Market, I wrote in Prothom Alo, ‘Chhatra League killed, BNP leader remanded.’ 

Both sides in the clash were public. But the police thought it was better to arrest the BNP leader and send him to remand than to find them. This time too, where the government investigation report revealed that the fire was caused by a short circuit, Awami League leaders are trying to find sabotage. 

I was surprised to notice that no matter what the fire or explosion was before Eid, the leaders of the government and opposition parties were looking for sabotage and conspiracy. But after Eid, neither side looked for conspiracy and sabotage in the incident where the smell spread through the gas supply line in Dhaka city. If sabotage takes a break during the Eid holidays, it is good news.

Headline_English: Hot water has been coming out of a deep tube well for three years
Content_English:
Hot water is being pumped from a 260-foot deep tube well to an electric motor. Daily work is being done with this water. The strange incident took place in Gilarchala village of Sreepur, Gazipur. Such hot water has been coming out of an electric motor-driven tube well in Shahab Uddin's house in that village for three years. 

As soon as the electric motor is turned on at any time, hot water starts coming out. Shahab Uddin's family members and tenants of the house, including 130 people, depend on the water from the tube well for daily work. Although it is convenient in winter, they have to face problems when using this water in hot days. However, the family members have now become accustomed to using this water for a long time. 

On Friday, it was seen on the spot that large drums and buckets were kept next to the tube well. Even though there is a water tap inside every toilet in Shahab Uddin's house, water has been stored in extra buckets. It was learned that the water is stored in these buckets for a long time to cool it down to make it suitable for use. 

The dyeing plant of Paramount Textile Mills Limited is located next to the tube well where it was installed. Shahab Uddin turned on the electric motor to show how hot the water was. He immediately put his hand in the water and felt it was as hot as the water in the geyser at home. 

The owner of the house, Shahab Uddin, said that about 18 years ago, he installed a 220-foot deep tube well in his house and was using water. Five years ago, the water in the tube well was found to have an unusual color. Later, he installed another tube well 10 feet away from this tube well. The depth of that tube well is 260 feet. Hot water started coming from this tube well three years ago. 

Shahab Uddin told Prothom Alo, "I have never seen such an incident of hot water coming out of a tube well anywhere. Everyone around is surprised. We don't even know why this is happening. We have to cool the hot water and use it. I don't even know if drinking this water will pose a health risk.' 

Talking to some residents of that house, it was learned that there is no way to use the water from the tube well for daily tasks, from cooking to bathing and toileting without cooling it. So, each of them has bought separate buckets and other water containers. Some people use ice buckets from the refrigerator to cool the water immediately for bathing. Residents said that after bathing in this water, the body feels a bit rough. 

Another resident of the house, Md. Kausar, said, 'There is a huge problem due to hot water. We have no way to solve this plight of hot water. We are forced to use this water in alternative ways.' 

Environmental activist Khorshed Alam described the issue of hot water coming out of the tube well as mysterious. He told Prothom Alo that this water should be tested. When informed about the matter, Assistant Engineer Md. Faisal Khan told Prothom Alo, "I have never heard of such an incident of hot water coming out from under the ground. The matter needs to be investigated. I will go there soon."

Headline_English: You will be surprised to know why mosquitoes hover near your ears!
Content_English:
The incidence of mosquitoes increases during summer and rainy days. This incidence seems to increase excessively when you go to sleep at dawn or at night. But do you know why most mosquitoes hang around near your ears? 
It is very difficult to find a person whose peaceful sleep at night has not been disturbed by the unbearable singing of mosquitoes. Even evening chats are ruined by this buzzing of mosquitoes. 

Experts say that such a nuisance of mosquitoes is seen everywhere, regardless of place, time, and place. However, mosquitoes hang around near people's ears more than anywhere else. 

However, the reason for this has been found in the explanation of science. Although there are several species of mosquitoes, Anopheles, Culex, Aedes, Hemagogues, but the female mosquito of the Anopheles species usually bites our body. 

Among these species, the large Culex species mosquito that lives in houses can be seen sitting on the walls of houses. However, these mosquitoes do not feed on human blood. They accumulate their necessary nutrition from the sap of leaves of trees or the nectar of flowers. Only female mosquitoes suck human blood. 

However, both male and female mosquitoes are seen hovering near human ears. Experts say that the reason for this is that mosquitoes are attracted to the carbon dioxide emitted from the human body and hover more near the ears. 

Through this carbon dioxide, mosquitoes can understand how many animals there may be in the house. The main reason why mosquitoes fly near the ears from other parts of the body is that the most carbon dioxide is emitted from our body right behind the nose, i.e. near the ears or at the back of the head. 

Biologists believe that mosquitoes do not have any special attraction to the ears. However, due to the high carbon dioxide, they fly closer to the ears under the guidance of their sensors. And that is when we hear the sound of their wings. 

Therefore, mosquitoes fly the most in these two places. Even after applying hair gel to the hair, mosquitoes continue to hover around the head due to its fragrance. 

The most amazing thing about mosquitoes is that the song that mosquitoes start singing when they come in front of your ears is not a mosquito song. Many people think that it is the sound of a mosquito's mouth. In fact, it is not. 

This sound is basically the sound of flapping its wings. Mosquitoes flap their wings about 90 thousand times in 3 seconds. And we consider this continuous flapping sound to be the unbearable song of mosquitoes.

Headline_English: You will be surprised to hear Sabina-Sanjidad's salary!
Content_English:
The country's football has ended its 19-year trophy drought thanks to Sabina. The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) is preparing to hold a grand reception to recognize their glorious achievement. But the question remains, will Sabina remain in the limelight after this? Will Sabina, who has brought Bangladesh one achievement after another despite Jamal Bhuiyan's failures, get the respect she deserves? 

The success story in women's football began in 2017. Maria Manda, Shamsunnahar, Tohura Khatun, Anai Mogini, Anuching Mogini, Monica Chakma and Rupna Chakma were flying the flag of excellence in Asian football from age-based football. Bangladesh won the title in the age-based SAFF Championship three times between 2017 and 2021 thanks to them. 

And in 2022, they made history by getting a chance in the national team. Under Sabina's leadership, Bangladesh won the first title in the Women's SAFF Championship. Earlier, this women's team had also defeated a strong team like Malaysia 6-0 in a friendly match. Whereas in 2022, Jamal Bhuiyan and his team were defeated by the same country by a margin of 1-4 goals. 

However, despite bringing so much success to the country, they are not given the due respect. The salary structure of women's football in the country is much less than that of a daily wage worker. You will be surprised to hear the salary structure of Sabina-Sanjidad! The monthly salary of 'A' category footballers is 12 thousand. The salaries of 'B' and 'C' category players are 10 thousand and 8 thousand. 

On the other hand, the footballers of the men's team are getting high salaries despite not being able to produce any results for a long time. The annual income of some Jamals exceeds crores of taka. However, the BFF is giving the excuse of the women's team's sponsor crisis as the reason for such discrimination. 

However, women do get some financial respect in club football. Bashundhara Kings pays the highest salary to women in club football. Whereas Sabina Khatun, Krishna Rani Sarkar and Sanjida Akhter get around 4-5 lakh taka depending on the category. That is also quite less than men. 

BFF President Kazi Salahuddin has, however, hinted at increasing women's salaries soon. It remains to be seen whether the girls who entered football with their mother's last possessions and sold their sister's jewelry can finally bring smiles to their families' faces.

Headline_English: Why are there fewer women in journalism in Bangladesh?
Content_English:
The time was 2015. 6 am. News came that Nilkanth Hajong, a member of the Bangladesh Army who was on the UN mission in Mali, had been shot dead by rebels. His village home was in a remote area of ​​Sunamganj. Upon hearing the news of the death of this tribal soldier, journalist Alpana Begum hurriedly left her house in Netrokona. Her motorbike accompanied her. 
This journey was not an ordinary journey. She had to cross a terribly difficult path from the Netrokona border towards Sunamganj. At that time, the Maheshkhola River was the most important. Apart from this, there were other rivers. There was a path to walk along the roots of trees. However, taking a motorbike also caused some difficulties. There were numerous canals or streams. BGB members had to cross them on foot. Since Alpana had a motorbike near her, she had to face a little trouble. 

Alpana Begum laughed as she spoke. She said, it is not possible to erase the memory of this journey from her mind. I fell down with my motorbike near the Maheshkhola River. Later, with the help of various BOPs, I was able to reach Nilkantha Hajong's house at around 4 pm. The relatives of the deceased soldier broke down in tears upon seeing us there. After collecting video footage from there and recording statements, I set off after evening. On the way back, it rained heavily and thundered. As a result, the hilly path became even more slippery. I crossed the Dharmapasha Madhyanagar boat. Later, I crossed at least three big rivers in the middle of Sunamganj Haor and returned home at around 3 am. She said, the place was so silent that I could not get any response from an area of ​​about 17 kilometers. 

Alpana Begum is a field journalist. She has been riding a motorbike in Netrokona for 22 years in search of new news. She has a motorbike. This machine is also her pet. It has been her companion for almost fourteen years. 

Journalism is valued as a challenging profession. Historically, both men and women have been attracted to this profession due to the uncertainty of the profession. Although men are seen to enter this profession more, women's participation is comparatively less in many places. Although women's journalism has progressed a lot in the socio-economic context of Bangladesh after independence, there are still some dark spots in the path of expansion of this profession due to obstacles and wrong values. 

Among the government universities, there are opportunities to pursue higher education in journalism at Dhaka, Chittagong and Rajshahi Universities. The Department of Journalism was launched at Dhaka University in 1962. Initially, it was part of the diploma course. The Department of Journalism was launched at Rajshahi University in 1993. At Chittagong University in 1994-95. To increase the promotion and expansion of journalism, the Department of Journalism and Media Studies of Jahangirnagar University started its journey in 2011. Among the private universities, journalism courses are available at Independent University, Daffodil University, University of Development Alternative, Stamford University, American International University of Bangladesh, etc. After graduating from these universities, students not only do journalism but also get the opportunity to build careers in various professions such as public relations, advertising agencies, film making, banking, and teaching. 

According to a report by the international media Deutsche Welle, the number of female journalists in Bangladesh has not increased much. Out of the 2,018 journalists of the National Press Club, only 72 are female journalists. In addition, out of the nearly 6,000 members of the Dhaka Union of Journalists, the number of female journalists is not more than 150. This is because many obstacles still remain. 

According to an estimate by the Global Media Monitoring Project, 8 percent of women journalists work in newspapers, 33 percent in radio, and 19 percent in television. However, women are found in presentation. More than 60 percent of radio or television presenters are women. However, women are still rarely seen in political, diplomatic, and economic reports. It is difficult to understand whether this is due to their inability to survive in the competition or their weakness in gender politics. 

We spoke to Nishat Parvez, an assistant professor at the Department of Journalism at Jahangirnagar University. He emphasized women's economic liberation and work environment security. Nishat said, "First of all, we have to think about whether there is room for economic liberation for women. Secondly, we have to keep in mind whether there is a safe environment for women to work. We have seen journalism as a male-dominated world so far. This perspective needs to change. Many are graduating from the journalism department. They are also teaching in these institutions. However, women are rarely seen in journalism. However, if you look, there is no safe work environment in journalism. There are some other issues. For example, the hashtag Me-Too movement starts every now and then. Then we saw what the situation was like.’ 

Nishat further told Soomi Sangbad that women are rarely seen at the top in some journalism houses. Women are given positions up to a certain level. They cannot go to higher levels. The authorities no longer want to show interest. If someone does go, they are also talked about, this has become a culture. 

He further said that after returning to the office after maternity leave, it is often seen that the reporter who was a reporter has become a newsroom editor. This is happening because of the lack of a working environment. There is also a common belief that girls need less money than boys. 

In response to the question of what can be done to improve the current situation, the teacher said that men also have to take responsibility here. A working environment has to be created. However, the quality of the working environment also varies due to the political environment or the overall situation of the country. Therefore, such a problem cannot be solved in a day. Various media houses also have to be more attentive to the issue of salaries and allowances of journalists. Even after graduating, many women and men receive very low salaries, which discourages them from pursuing a career in this profession. 

Angur Nahar Monti, former president of Diplomatic Correspondents Association Bangladesh and coordinator of Women Journalist Network Bangladesh (WJNB), General Secretary, shared her experience with Soomi Sangbad. She said, "When it comes to women's empowerment, we have come a long way in Bangladesh. Many examples can be given where women are ahead. We are proud of this globally as well. However, it is also true that women have not come much forward in the field of women's journalism. Women are sometimes seen as 'victims' and sometimes as 'products' in the media. But there is also an opposite picture. Women are doing extraordinary work. But they are not getting results accordingly. 

We also had to wait a long time to get a woman president of the National Press Club. Besides, those who come to this profession, they come knowing the risks of this profession. Both men and women have to accept this challenge or risk. However, it is more difficult for women. Apart from that, the salary and allowances are also low. We talk so much about ethics, yet sexual harassment and other discrimination still exist in our workplace. Women are victims of many subtle discriminations. There is still little room for mutual respect. 

However, this journalist did not give up hope. She said, we have many achievements. And I see this well that more women are working in presentation. Because, this also requires knowledge of journalism. We have to remember that women do not need pity in the workplace. They do not need any additional benefits. Women need to be made aware of their rights. 

At the beginning of the report, the story of Netrokona journalist Alpana Begum was being told. Like Nishat Parvez and Angur Nahar Monti, she also believes that women who come to work in the media are still lagging behind due to limited opportunities. She also highlighted the additional difficulties of being women. However, she also said that women should be more determined to come forward.

Headline_English: Why is India reluctant to invite Bangladesh?
Content_English:
The government of India invites one foreign head of state as the chief guest to the Republic Day ceremony every year. This tradition has been going on since 1950. India's arch-enemy Pakistan and even China have been included in this list. However, no head of state from Bangladesh has been invited to the ceremony so far. But why? 

India's Republic Day or Republic Day is on January 26. This year, the country is celebrating its 74th Republic Day. Although the country gained independence in 1947, India became a democratic state when the Constitution came into effect in the Indian Constituent Assembly on January 26, 1950. However, just two months before it came into effect, the Constitution of India was approved by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. 

The Indian government decided after a long discussion who would be the chief guest of the Republic Day. In this case, the country gives its own diplomatic interests the highest priority. Various issues including the political, economic and commercial relations of India with its neighboring countries are taken into consideration. And in these cases, the friendly relations between Dhaka and Delhi are well known. But despite that, India is mysteriously indifferent to inviting any head of state from Bangladesh as the chief guest at the Republic Day ceremony. 

The heads of state of Congo, Tobago, and Zambia are also among those who have found a place in the list of foreign guests at the Republic Day ceremony in India. The head of state of France has attended the most (five times). The heads of state of Bhutan and Russia have attended four times each. 

Among the countries of South and Central Asia, India's archenemy Pakistan has also got the opportunity to attend twice. China, with which there is a constant bloody war on the border, has also been invited once. In addition, Sri Lanka has joined twice, and countries like Myanmar, Maldives, Afghanistan, and Kazakhstan have joined once each. 

There are also examples of multiple heads of state and government being 'guests of honor' in this parade. For example, six people were made guests of honor in 2017. In addition, the following year, i.e. in 2018, the leaders of 10 ASEAN countries, including Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi, were invited as special guests at the Republic Day ceremony, breaking the tradition. 

But no head of state from Bangladesh, which has the title of the most 'close friend', has ever been invited to India's Republic Day ceremony. Naturally, the question arises, why was the President or Prime Minister of a country whose independence war India actively participated in, and which India recognizes as its 'most trusted and reliable neighbor', not given the status of special guest on Republic Day? When Bangladesh is a role model of development in the world, what is the reason for India's reluctance to invite the country's heads of state? 
Among the SAARC member states, all but one, Bangladesh, have been guests on India's Republic Day. 

Those concerned say that the safe 'Seven Sisters' are the contribution of the Bangladesh government. In addition, Bangladesh has been continuously cooperating with India in various other areas. Many are therefore raising questions, why is this neglect towards Dhaka despite all this? Does India consider Bangladesh its main rival in the geopolitical context? Or is it because of a violent attitude that no head of state from Bangladesh is made the chief guest at the Republic Day ceremony? 

In 2019, at an informal meeting in Delhi, India, journalists, politicians and the then Minister of State for External Affairs of India, MJ Akbar, were asked about this. Somewhat evasively, he said, ‘Bangladesh was not (a guest), it will be’. 

It is learned that Matiur Rahman, editor of the Daily Prothom Alo, Mahfuz Anam, editor of the English daily The Daily Star, and eight other heads of television and newspapers were present at the meeting. Although Daily Star editor Mahfuz Anam was contacted on his mobile phone to inquire about this, he did not agree to talk to Soom Sangbad. 

Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson was supposed to be the chief guest at the 72nd Republic Day ceremony in 2021. However, he canceled his visit to India due to the worsening Corona situation. For the same reason, India did not invite any foreign guest to the Republic Day ceremony in 2022. 

However, members of the Bangladesh Armed Forces were at the forefront of India's 72nd Republic Day parade on the streets of Delhi. On January 26 of that year, a 122-member contingent of Bangladesh's three services inaugurated the colorful Republic Day parade. Through their parade, the golden jubilee of Bangladesh's independence and the birth centenary of the Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman were commemorated, along with remembering the freedom fighters. 

However, questions were still raised from various quarters that why the government, which has been making various statements and disparaging Bangladesh at various times, suddenly honored Bangladesh with this rare recognition? 

At that time, the Indian Army announced that it would give special honors to Bangladesh on the 72nd Republic Day as part of the 'Golden Jubilee' that the whole of India celebrated on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of the Liberation War of 1971. 

But despite this special honor or friendly relationship, not inviting any Bangladeshi head of state to the Republic Day ceremony raises questions about India's foreign policy. Former Indian ambassador to Bangladesh Dev Mukherjee believes that this is actually a 'paradox' or enigma of India's foreign policy. In an interview with the media, he said, 'The problem is that India's foreign policy is incomprehensible. Although the responsibility lies with India as a 'big neighbor'.' 

Analysts also do not deny that Bangladesh has been helping India in various important areas. In the words of Nayinima Basu, diplomatic editor of India's The Print Portal, 'Whether it is expelling the separatists from the northeast or handing them over to India - the way this Bangladesh government has helped India is incomparable. As a result, cooperation should be mutual.’ 

Read more: India-Bangladesh border much better than before: Minister of State for Shipping 

Still, it is still unclear where exactly Delhi’s reluctance to invite a Bangladeshi head of state to an event like Republic Day lies. 

What is happening in this year’s event 

After two years, West Bengal is joining the Republic Day parade in Delhi. Although West Bengal has been accused of being deprived of the Republic Day ceremony in Delhi in the past, the state has significantly got a place in the parade this year. 

Like last year, this year too, India’s Republic Day celebrations began on January 23 and will end on January 30. This time, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, known as a dictator, is being the chief guest at the country’s Republic Day ceremony. 

This time, 120 members of the Egyptian armed forces are participating in India’s Republic Day parade. Like last year, workers employed in the project have been invited as guests in the Republic Day parade. Who have been named 'Shramyogi'. 

However, this time the central government of the country has made a huge cut in the invitations of VIPs and other officials, according to local media. Last year, the total number of seats including VIPs and officials was one lakh. This time it has been reduced to 45 thousand.

Headline_English: What's happening in Khagrachari, what's happened so far
Content_English:
Tension has been prevailing in Khagrachhari for the past five days (Wednesday to Sunday) in protest against the alleged gang rape of a teenage girl. Clashes and brickbats also took place during the road blockade. The administration finally imposed Section 144 for an indefinite period to bring the situation under control. Meanwhile, arson and clashes occurred in the Guimara Bazaar in the Upazila next to Khagrachhari Sadar. Finally, three people were killed in the shooting on Sunday. At least 20 people, including army personnel and police, were injured. 

The Khagrachhari district town is now at a standstill. All shops are closed. There is panic among the people. However, the police say that the situation is under control. Meanwhile, the Jumma Chhatra-Janta announced today that they will continue their program, including an indefinite road blockade, until their demands are met. This was announced in a statement posted on the Facebook page Jumma Chhatra-Janta. In it, they made eight-point demands. 

How the incident began 
A schoolgirl was gang-raped on her way back from private school at 9 pm last Tuesday. Her relatives rescued her unconscious from a field around 11 pm that day. Police have arrested one person on charges of involvement in the incident after the girl's father filed a case. His name is Shayan Shil (21). The court has ordered a six-day remand for him. 

The next day, from Wednesday, the Jumma students and the public started a movement to protest the rape. On their call, a half-day road blockade program was held on Thursday. Later, the protesters held a rally against oppression of women on Friday. 

Aware students, youth and civil society protested in Khagrachhari demanding justice for the gang rape of a hill girl. Today at 5 pm in the Cheragi Pahar Mor area of ​​Chittagong city 
Aware students, youth and civil society protested in Khagrachhari demanding justice for the gang rape of a hill girl. Today at 5 pm in the Cheragi Pahar Mor area of ​​Chittagong city Photo: Sourav Das 
There was no program on Friday. However, a morning-evening blockade was called the next day, Saturday. On that day, a local group clashed with the blockaders at the Sadar Upazila Parishad premises and threw bricks. It was claimed that four people from both sides were injured. Later, security forces went to control the situation, but clashes broke out again in the Mahajanpara area of ​​the city at around 4 pm. At that time, shops were vandalized in various areas including Mahajanpara and Narkelbagan. Clashes and clashes broke out in four places in the Sadar from 12:30 pm to 4 pm that day. 

To bring the situation under control, the administration imposed Section 144 in the Sadar, the municipal area and Guimara after 2 pm on Saturday. 

Videos and pictures of the market being set on fire were spread on social media Facebook. In the video, shops in the market can be seen burning in the fire. Most of the shopkeepers in the market are said to be from the hills. After this incident, the situation in Guimara upazila of Khagrachari was tense. Law enforcement forces were patrolling the area. Earlier in the afternoon, there was a clash between members of the law enforcement agencies and those supporting the blockade. Gunfire was heard at that time. 

Eyewitnesses Mangsazai Marma and Kanjari Marma said that they were peacefully protesting on the road in front of the food warehouse in support of the blockade. At that time, they had an argument with the law enforcement agencies when they arrived. At one point in the argument, the two alleged that the law enforcement agencies opened fire on them. They said that immediately after the gunshots, people fled in fear. Then 20-25 people came and looted Ramesu Bazar and houses and set them on fire as they left. There were also masked people with these people. At that time, shops and houses were also set on fire. 

Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) of Chittagong Range Ahsan Habib Palash confirmed to Prothom Alo that three people died in the gunfire. This evening, he told Prothom Alo that three people were killed in a shooting in Guimara. Their bodies are in the hospital. However, details of who shot them and how they died are not known. He also said that in addition to the three people killed in the shooting, three others were injured. 

When asked about this, Khagrachari District Civil Surgeon Mohammad Saber told Prothom Alo that the bodies of three men from Guimara have arrived at Khagrachari District Hospital. Their bodies have been kept in the morgue. An autopsy will be performed tomorrow, Monday morning. He also said that the four injured people brought from Guimara are undergoing treatment at the hospital. 

The identities of the three injured have been known. They are Bikash Tripura (26), Chingkeu Marma (26) and Ugya Marma (22). They are undergoing treatment at Khagrachari District Hospital. Of these, Chingkeu Marma was shot in the left knee and came out through the other side. Hospital sources said that the condition of the three is normal. 

A statement sent by the Home Ministry also informed about the deaths of three hillmen. It said that the Ministry of Home Affairs has expressed deep sorrow over the incident in which three hillmen were killed and 13 army personnel including a major, three policemen including the OC of Guimara Police Station and many others were injured in the attack by miscreants in Guimara Upazila of Khagrachari district. In a statement, the ministry assured that legal action will be taken against those involved in the incident after investigation very soon. No criminal will be spared. Until then, the ministry has requested all concerned to remain patient and calm. 

There is a third party's fuel: Supradeep Chakma 
At a view-exchange meeting organized at the conference room of the Khagrachari district administration this afternoon, Advisor on Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs Supradeep Chakma said that there is a third party's fuel in the ongoing situation in Khagrachari. He said that a party is trying to obstruct the election by creating violence in the name of movement. At this time, he warned of taking action against illegal arms holders in the hills. 

Today, they are trying to create an unstable situation in the hills by creating new issues. The main challenge for the government is to hold elections. If anyone tries to sabotage the elections, action will be taken against them. No new issues will be allowed to be created. From now on, no one will be able to hold processions or meetings without the permission of the administration. Senior law enforcement officers, representatives of political, social and civil organizations participated in the meeting. 

Khagrachhari in a hurry, Khagrachhari-bound passengers stuck 
4:30 pm on Sunday. Oxygen area of ​​Chittagong city. Khagrachhari bus counter is next to the road. There is a crowd of people there. They are standing in front of the counter, waiting for the bus. The bus was standing next to it. But no one knows when it will leave. The counter staff and the passengers got into a fight over this. 

One of the passengers is Sakhawat Hossain. He lives in Matiranga. He does farming. He came to visit his daughter's house in the city's Oxygen area three days ago. Today, he came to the bus counter to return to his village home, Matiranga, Khagrachari. 

Sakhawat told Prothom Alo at 4:30 pm on Sunday that he has been standing for two and a half to three hours. The bus is saying it will come, but it does not. There is a fight in Guimara. Because of this, the people at the counter cannot say for sure whether it will go or not. Even if it does, he is waiting. He will wait for a while longer. If he does not get a car, he will return to his daughter's house. 

The person at the counter said that there is trouble in Khagrachari. Barricades and trees have been thrown down on the road. In this situation, it is not possible to go by car. Even then, he is trying to take the bus. But it does not seem possible. 

A couple was waiting for the car. They were going to go to their village home, Matiranga, for a puja. However, according to them, it seems that they will not be able to go after looking at the situation. In the end, they could not go. 

On the other hand, the situation in Khagrachari city has been tense since this morning. Security forces were stationed at every corner of the city. No shops were opened in and around the market. Security forces are questioning those who are going out for essential work.

Headline_English: Ronaldo surpasses Messi
Content_English:
The age is almost 40. The footballer who once dominated the European league is currently playing in the Saudi Pro League. However, the star footballer's edge has not diminished at all, as can be seen from his recent performance. The Portuguese superstar scored a hat-trick in two consecutive matches in the Saudi Pro League. 
On Tuesday (April 2), Al Nasr faced Ava Club in the Saudi Pro League match. Al Nasr scored five goals in the Ava net in the first half of the match. Ronaldo completed the hat-trick in the first half. This is his 65th hat-trick in his football career. 
Ronaldo surpassed his arch-rival Messi with this hat-trick. Messi is behind Ronaldo in both club and national team hat-tricks. Messi has scored a total of 57 hat-tricks in his football career so far. Of these, 48 were for clubs, the remaining 9 were for national teams. Ronaldo has 10 hat-tricks in his national team. He has scored three or more goals 55 times in the jerseys of different clubs. 

Ronaldo contributed to all five goals in the first half against Ava. The Portuguese superstar provided excellent assists in the remaining two goals, except for his own three. 

Ronaldo scored his first goal in the 11th minute of the match at the Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Stadium. The Portuguese superstar's second goal came in the 21st minute. Senegalese star Sadio Mane scored the third goal for the team. Ronaldo provided the ball for his goal in the 33rd minute. Ronaldo completed his hat-trick by scoring the team's fourth and his third goal in the 42nd minute. Ronaldo also assisted Al Sulaihim's goal two minutes later.

Headline_English: This is why Ukraine is killing its own soldiers
Content_English:
An Ilyushin Il-76 passenger plane was shot down in Russian airspace on Wednesday (January 24). All 65 Ukrainian prisoners of war, three Russian military guards and six crew members on board were killed. The plane is believed to have been shot down by a Patriot missile system supplied to Ukraine by the United States. 

The question is, what were Ukrainian soldiers doing so far from their homeland? The answer is that these soldiers were detained in the Luhansk and Donetsk regions of Russia, and later on July 29, 2022, a Ukrainian HIMARS missile attack on a prison camp in the Olenivka region killed 53 people. The prisoners of war killed on Wednesday were being evacuated to distance Ukrainian prisoners of war from the high-tech weapons provided to Ukraine by NATO. 
But this Russian tactic did not work. Ukraine has once again proven how dangerous they can be to their own citizens. 

The attack took place on Wednesday afternoon local time. After the attack, the Ukrainian government's Telegram channel reported that the plane was carrying Russian S-300 missiles for an attack on the Kharkiv region. Shortly after, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced that 65 Ukrainian prisoners of war were on board, but the news of the missiles being carried was deleted from the Ukrainian Telegram channel. News coverage 

As usual, Ukraine is denying the accusations that its soldiers were killed, which means that it seems unlikely to know why it carried out the attack anytime soon. The attack could be either a mistake by the Ukrainian military or an attempt to provoke Russia. However, this incident will not stop Russia from exchanging prisoners of war. Although about 1,000 Russian prisoners of war have been returned from Ukraine in the past two years, many more Russian soldiers are still being held in Ukraine. A prisoner exchange is needed to get them back. 
The Ukrainian military, which is weakening day by day, is no longer fighting in the hope of a better future or independence, because the Ukrainian military authorities have admitted that Russia gave them a number of favorable conditions in March and April 2022. 

Ukraine is not fighting to expel the enemy, because only a madman would hope that Ukraine has the ability to defeat Russia. 

Ukraine is not fighting to become part of Europe, because Western countries have begun to back down from the process of Ukraine becoming part of NATO. 

Ukraine is fighting only to keep Volodymyr Zelensky in power.

Headline_English: Opportunity to make toilet tissue from ex's love letters
Content_English:

Headline_English: You'll be surprised to know the reason why you check your phone every now and then
Content_English:
The one thing that is difficult to spend a day without nowadays is your smartphone. And the reason why you can't stop checking your phone every now and then is the 'attention economy'. 

The one thing that is difficult to spend a day without nowadays is your smartphone 
There is now infinite information at your fingertips. Everyone wants to earn money through your attention. So everything you see on your smartphone is arranged in a way that is bound to attract your attention. Because here, someone is benefiting economically from everything you see, like or comment on, and from all the necessary and unnecessary things you buy. Here, your time and attention are valuable assets. 

Billions of dollars of business are going on online in exchange for the time and attention of millions of people like you. And this is called the attention economy, where everyone is busy earning money by attracting your attention. That is exactly why you can't stop checking your phone every now and then. 

In this digital age of the 21st century, whatever streaming services, reels, videos, audios or advertisements you watch or listen to, are all designed in such a way that they attract your attention and others do business through them. 
The internet is full of infinite information and advertisements. But your time and attention are limited. So, the competition is on to enjoy the most information and services in the shortest time. 

The algorithms of social media and online sites are working in various ways all the time to keep your attention for the longest time. By using artificial intelligence and creating personalized content for you, ‘psychological manipulation’ is being brought to the fore. By constantly monitoring what kind of content you enjoy, you are being shown more and more of that kind of content. So that your attention does not move away from the screen. 
Other people's businesses are running by using your attention. Others are making money on the basis of popularity. Your attention, time, and even you yourself are being used as a commodity without your knowledge. Although various parties are making money through this, everything from your normal family, social and professional life to your mental health is being damaged. Who knows where this uncontrolled scrolling will end! So control yourself before you are controlled.

Headline_English: Does car-crazy Mbappe have a driving license? You will be surprised to know this information

Headline_English: Where the clock turns counterclockwise
Content_English:
The clock is at 11 o'clock. According to the conventional rule, it will strike 12 o'clock after 1 hour. But suddenly you see that instead of 12 o'clock, the clock is about to strike 10 o'clock. You will surely be surprised. Such a surprising phenomenon can be seen if you go to an area inhabited by people of small ethnic groups in India. There, the clock does not rotate according to the conventional rule, but rotates in reverse. That is, instead of going from left to right, it runs from right to left. 

India Times reported in a report last Sunday that the people of the small ethnic group Gand community live in a remote area of ​​​​Kori district in northern Chhattisgarh. The rule there is that the clock will run in reverse. That is, after 10 o'clock, the clock will not run towards 11 o'clock; rather, it will fall behind 10 o'clock. 

So it is not that the clock is telling the wrong time. The villagers have adjusted their lives and activities by seeing the time in reverse this way. 

But why this exceptional and strange rule? According to the news, the people of that community believe that the world moves counterclockwise. That is, it moves from right to left continuously. Therefore, the hands of the clock should also move from right to left. If the hands of the clock move from left to right, then it will conflict with the laws of nature. This is an evil, unnatural act. It can harm them. Therefore, they have introduced such an exceptional rule since 2008.

Headline_English: Why menthol cigarettes are so important in the Trump-Biden duel
Content_English:
The presidential election in the United States is going to be held in November. If all goes well, current President Joe Biden and former President Donald Trump will face each other. Surprisingly, cigarettes have become an important factor in this Trump-Biden duel. More specifically, menthol cigarettes. 

Menthol cigarettes are quite popular among African-Americans. But the Joe Biden administration wants to ban these cigarettes. Discussions are also underway regarding a proposal in this regard. And this discussion is gaining special importance in an election year. 

African Americans are known to be supporters of Biden's Democratic Party. But many of them are quite upset with such an initiative by the Biden administration. Therefore, it is believed that such an initiative could have a major impact on Biden's ballot box. 

In South Carolina, a conservative group called 'Building America's Future' sent a letter to about 75,000 Democratic voters last February. In the letter, they urged them not to vote for Joe Biden in the state's primary. Biden's initiative to ban menthol cigarettes is cited as the reason. 

In addition, the attitude of influential groups associated with the tobacco business in the United States has aroused fear. It is believed that this ban could lead to the spread of policing and racism in the country. At the same time, the Republican Party can use this issue to win the hearts of black voters in the election year. 

The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced a draft plan in 2022. It announced the ban on the production and sale of specially flavored tobacco. According to the FDA, this will discourage future smokers. And it will also benefit those who want to quit smoking. 

Biden had given the green light to implement this central rule last year. But its implementation was suspended until this March due to concerns that there might be a backlash among black voters. In this situation, anti-tobacco campaigners fear that the rule may not be implemented anymore. 

Black smokers in the United States buy more menthol cigarettes than white smokers. Therefore, many involved in the tobacco industry in the country believe that if the Biden administration makes such a decision, it will create a reaction among black smokers in the United States. 

It is uncertain what decision President Joe Biden will ultimately make on this in an election year. But health experts are strongly criticizing such a delay. According to FDA data, about 500,000 people die from smoking-related illnesses in the United States every year. 
8 out of 10 African-American smokers buy menthol cigarettes. They smoke with these cigarettes. On the other hand, only 3 out of 10 white smokers smoke with menthol cigarettes. 

Civil rights activist Al Sharpton is a staunch opponent of such an initiative by the Biden administration. He said at an event in 2019, ‘Smoking is not good for you. There is no question about it. But if it's about health awareness, why don't you ban all types of cigarettes?' 

Al Sharpton wrote a letter to the White House about the FDA's proposal. In the letter, he wrote that banning menthol cigarettes could exacerbate existing problems in American society with racial profiling, discrimination, and policing. 

Politico reports that a statewide ban was proposed in New York last year. The famous rights activist put pressure on him in the letter. 

Now, with the presidential election approaching, Republicans are looking at the issue to attract important black voters to the ballot box. 

In South Carolina, a conservative group called 'Building America's Future' sent a letter to about 75,000 Democratic voters last February. In the letter, they urged them not to vote for Joe Biden in the state's primary. Biden's initiative to ban menthol cigarettes was cited as the reason.

Building America's Future has run an ad on this. It says that Biden should focus on bigger priorities instead of talking about what adults can and can't do. 

Altria, the owner of several popular cigarette brands including Marlboro, conducted a survey last year. That survey also found that minority voters could turn against Joe Biden at the polls if menthol cigarettes were banned. 

Although other surveys have shown that most black voters support the ban. 

It is uncertain what President Biden will ultimately decide on this in an election year. But health experts are strongly criticizing such a delay. Because according to the FDA, about 500,000 people die each year in the United States from smoking-related illnesses. 

In this regard, Emily Holubowicz of the American Heart Association told Biden, "The closer you get to the election, the closer the hard things get. But it's the right thing to do." History is on your side. Public health is on your side. 

NAACP President Derrick Johnson is in favor of banning menthol cigarettes. He calls on the White House to focus on science, research, and the health of African-Americans. 
The European Union (EU) banned the sale of menthol cigarettes in 2020. Later, similar rules were introduced in the US states of California and Massachusetts.

Headline_English: Judge's comment is unconstitutional, says he has turned the country into hell
Content_English:
Attorney General Abu Mohammad AM Amin Uddin has termed the High Court judge's remark that he has 'turned the country into hell' as unconstitutional and disrespectful. 

He made the comment in response to questions from journalists at the Attorney General's office on Tuesday (October 10).

I don't know whether the various classes and groups are saying things as part of the conspiracy of the judiciary, whether he (the judge) has asked them to benefit through his words, we need to investigate. 

Earlier, the appeal and bail application of Adilur and Nasir, who were sentenced to prison in a case filed under the Information Technology Act, was presented by senior lawyer AJ Mohammad Ali to the bench of Justice Md. Emdadul Haque Azad. 

At that time, Deputy Attorney General (DAG) Md. Rezaul Karim opposed the bail application. He told the court that the state party has arguments against the bail application. 

Justice Md. Emdadul Haque expressed his anger at the state party's opposition in the bail hearing. He said, then why did you give them a 2-year sentence? Couldn't you give them a life sentence? You have turned the country into hell.

Headline_English: You'll be surprised to know who are easy targets for pickpockets
Content_English:
A post by a content creator named Lewis Gunson on Instagram is going viral. The title of the post is ‘I asked a pickpocket who they target. I immediately changed my jacket after hearing the answer.’ The post has already received 12 million views. Lewis recently spoke to a pickpocket. Lewis asked the pickpocket who they (pickpockets) target? Knowing the answer will make you think twice before going out. 
Pickpockets target those who are busy on their phones. Photo: Free Pick 
You might think that pickpockets target those who look rich. In fact, pickpockets usually target people who are the easiest to steal from. They don’t look at whether they ‘look rich’, but rather, who is the most careless. Find out who pickpockets usually pickpocket. 

Many people easily become victims of pickpockets because they are busy with other things and do not pay attention to their surroundings. 
Many people easily become victims of pickpockets because they are busy with other things and do not pay attention to their surroundings. Photo: Free Pick 
1. Those who are busy with their phones 
If they check their phones repeatedly or are immersed in their phones while walking, they do not pay attention to other things. And pickpockets do not fail to take advantage of those weak moments. 

2. Those who keep money in their back pockets or have their bag chains untied 
Keeping a mobile phone, wallet or money in their back pockets means silently inviting pickpockets. The pickpocket that Lewis interviewed said, 'We think that whatever is in our back pockets is ours. And opening someone else's bag chain means that it is completely free for us! The one who (the pickpocket) could not take it, that is his complete failure.’ 

The group and the inattentive are one of the easiest targets for pickpockets 
The group and the inattentive are one of the easiest targets for pickpockets Photo: Free Pick 
3. Those who wear loose clothes or jackets 
Because it is easy to slip your hand into loose clothes and take something quickly. Again, it is difficult for the victims to notice. 

4. Those who look worried or confused 
Because they are busy with something else, many people easily become victims of pickpockets. 

5. Those who are always busy 
When you are in a hurry, you do not look around, you do not pay attention. Pickpockets seize that opportunity.

Headline_English: Do you know who is happier after the age of 60?
Content_English:
We often think of happiness as something that is a goal that has to be achieved. But after sixty, many people start to understand that happiness is not really a goal. Ordinary life is valuable. 
My great aunt is 63 years old. It has been four years since my uncle passed away. My aunt's children are established. After fulfilling all the responsibilities of her entire life, my aunt is kind of retired. 

I returned from my great aunt's house in Shailkupa, Jhenaidah at the beginning of winter. The house is tidy, tip-top. She is weaving a Kurush pattern for her daughter-in-law's maxi. 

She also gifted a Kurush pattern for my three-year-old daughter's frock. She had already made it when she heard that we were going on a trip. 

Even at this age, she is sewing a Nakshi Kantha with glasses on her eyes. She has planted coriander, mint, several varieties of chili and a few other plants in the balcony tub. In a small area in front of the house, there is a gourd, pumpkin, and bitter gourd. There are tomatoes and a few other vegetables there. 

My aunt is diabetic and she walks regularly with a young woman from the next house after Fajr prayers. In the evening, that girl comes and puts oil on my aunt's hair. She helps with small tasks. She talks. When we returned, she made a big box of nadu. Even though she said, "Here we are," she seemed to be quite well. 

I usually finish my Eid shopping at the beginning of Ramadan to avoid the crowds and cool off for Eid shopping. This time too, I met a couple while shopping for Eid. They are between 65 and 75 years old. 

The only younger daughter, son-in-law and two granddaughters are coming from Canada. So this Eid is different for this couple. 

When she saw my daughter, she said, "My youngest granddaughter is the same age as your daughter, she will be 3 in April. This time, her birthday will be at our house." You know, this is the first time we will meet face to face.’ 

He bought two identical pairs of frocks for his two granddaughters from a famous local folk art shop in Jessore. He bought a handmade lace curtain to gift to his daughter. He ordered various other things. 
The two elderly men were walking around looking at various things and asking this and that. He said that they would go to the supermarket for a coffee break. For a week, the two of them had been walking around Jessore together, buying various things to cook and eat. 

They had also made a list of what they would cook on a certain day, where they would go for a walk. It seemed that there was no hesitation or pressure between the two of them. 

Two sons live in Dhaka and the only daughter is in Canada. The children asked them to stay with them. But the two said that they like to live in their old house in their own way. As a result, they spend a large part of their day on video calls. 

They don’t have much expectation from anyone. They are happy with what they have. I saw the two of them making small decisions together. Fulfilling their hobbies and being content. 
We often think of happiness as something that is a goal that has to be achieved. But after sixty, many people begin to understand that happiness is not really a goal. Ordinary life is valuable. Slow living, slowly enjoying small tasks, gradually, and peacefully, also has happiness. 

Many people think throughout their lives, ‘I will be happy if I get a promotion at work’ or ‘I will be happy if I accumulate a certain amount of money, buy a house or a car’. The problem with this idea is that if happiness is made a goal, the race never ends. The distance to the goal keeps increasing. And we run and run, panting. 

Happiness is not the only meaningful thing in human life. As people grow older, they learn to value peace over excitement, satisfaction over success, and status or the present moment over achievement.

Last word 
The happiest people after sixty have not always found a big purpose. Rather, they have understood one important thing. Happiness is not something to be achieved. 

Life has to be accepted as it is. Excessive or unwanted expectations do not make you happy, but rather take a U-turn on the road to happiness and throw you far away from it.

When people stop seeing each day as a test or a list of achievements, they realize that a simple morning with birdsong, a quiet afternoon, a simple evening with tea and biscuits, a day without regrets, and living in the present—these are often enough to make them happy.
